No Yasu? Well that makes explaining certain lore involving HOPE a lot more complicated. I could keep listing examples, but you get the idea.

I just couldn’t see Lessons in Love without the cast we have. They’re all amazing in one way or another.

LoveRedHairedGirl said:

Would you press the button to change the timeline? If so, why?
Click to expand...
I'd have to say no, mostly because it'd might as well be just a generic Dating Sim, then, tbh. Most of the drama and backstory comes from the second floor. The game would surely suffer if it's just variations of Chapter 1 ad nauseam.

Assuming the game continued without the school collasping then it'd likely become a dead end:
No Sensei had survived past the 3rd Reset, until the School collapsed and the Dorm Wars happened, according to Maya. Without the Nakayamas, Sensei would likely never regain any memories, so either he'd be Reset, or Maya would become desperate and probably just break him eventually (she'd probably not become how she did in Chapter 2). Or Ami might just go psycho, since she apparently only did that before the transfers according to Maya. Basically the game would start ending after Chapter 1.

If the characters still exist but never joined the class, then we'd probably just get worse versions of them. Some would still be involved but have less reason to be, or to grow.

Kirin and Yasu wouldn't have Noriko or Touka to rein them in. Nodoka would basically care even less about people. Noriko would be looking for Sensei forever. Etc. Otoha might still date and cheat on Rin, but she might have a school girl harem on her end, and Rin might end up cutting herself more and more.

The majority of the game would feel a whole lot more repetitive, with the girls themselves probably becoming boring or annoying. We'd be relating to Maya Prime more.
Overall: What might have happened if Maya never held Sensei's hands:
Maya - "Actually..."
- "Give me your hands."
Sensei Narrator - "But something about the way her hands begin to hold onto mine a little tighter tells me that-"
(Chapter 1 'Changing of Seasons' Main Event)

*later that night*
Rin - "My friend's school just..."
- "Collapsed."
- "You never know when shit like that is just going to happen."
Maya - "It's not supposed to."
(Chapter 2 'Fireworks, Chicken, and the Innate Fear of Death' Main Event)

*later, after the first Dorm Wars*
Maya - "Last time, I was an absolute idiot and let my mind get crowded during the process. Which may or may not have led to the destruction of an entire school."
(Chapter 2 'Record Breaker' Main Event)
Respect the power of handholding.

I'd have to say no, mostly because it'd might as well be just a generic Dating Sim, then, tbh. Most of the drama and backstory comes from the second floor. The game would surely suffer if it's just variations of Chapter 1 ad nauseam.

Assuming the game continued without the school collasping then it'd likely become a dead end:
No Sensei had survived past the 3rd Reset, until the School collapsed and the Dorm Wars happened, according to Maya. Without the Nakayamas, Sensei would likely never regain any memories, so either he'd be Reset, or Maya would become desperate and probably just break him eventually (she'd probably not become how she did in Chapter 2). Or Ami might just go psycho, since she apparently only did that before the transfers according to Maya. Basically the game would start ending after Chapter 1.

If the characters still exist but never joined the class, then we'd probably just get worse versions of them. Some would still be involved but have less reason to be, or to grow.

Kirin and Yasu wouldn't have Noriko or Touka to rein them in. Nodoka would basically care even less about people. Noriko would be looking for Sensei forever. Etc. Otoha might still date and cheat on Rin, but she might have a school girl harem on her end, and Rin might end up cutting herself more and more.

The majority of the game would feel a whole lot more repetitive, with the girls themselves probably becoming boring or annoying. We'd be relating to Maya Prime more.

posts.content_html_raw:
Well i finished chapter 3 and i gotta say,it was peak.It made me laugh but most of all it made me cry.(Metaphorically,not literally.That will be reserved for
When Maya prime comes back

Anyways having to go through Maya Primes pop was painful but man did i love it.Chapter 3 truly brought us peak writing.Surely chapter 4 will also be as good right? jej



Anyways leaving the sob story aside let me include the necessary lore screenshot that i will revisit later.



Now this,not having finished all the game yet and potentially missing a new piece of the puzzle,is very curious.I wont go too deep into it here but i weill just state that the concept of someone making a wish has now been mentioned 2.5 times(Involunterly wishing well pun)(Also i say 2.5 since i *think* ami said smt like that in the backwards bus but i need to replay to be sure).

Anyways the first time was Maya saying so in the 4th? reset,back when she suddenly appeared in her dorm room bed and jumped unto akiras arms(very cute).

The second was this.

Now my memory is not great and the prolonged abstinence hasnt helped but i do believe someone in this thread briefly had a discussion about the wishing well and its connection with the way Maya reset/s the world.I wont try to make any claims rn since i just wanna make an organized collection of the more obscure parts of the lore,such as Nib/Upside down house lore cause for some reason its a thing.One think i am curious and i want to talk about in the future though is something ill just refer to as "Eggs,spiders and butterflies" because the game has been hitting me on the face with these things for quite some time now and im tired of ignoring what,to be perfectly honest,might just be some silly symbolism that Sel decided to include to feel good about himself.Anyways rant over.Conclusion is this:Chapter 3 is peak,Maya is best girl and she will NEVER be overthrown,Wakana and touka grew to be very lovable characters and climbed my rankings a lot(still cant suprasse the the big 4,Maya ayane ami nodoka but they try).Praise be!

this is a repeat of something I've said a few times, but I really hope it isn't revealed that Nozomu raped Akira.

I feel like it would really undermine what Sekai did, and make it kind of unrealistic that Akira even resented Nozomu for fucking/owning the woman he loved, when the act of having previously raped him would (imo) be of a much higher priority than that.

Now, if it is revealed that Nozomu wanted to rape Akira, that's fine. It's also something I've theorized about the possibility of him being jealous of Akira, rather than of Sekai in episodes like what Ami described about her scent. Maybe even to the possibility of Nozomu trying to kill her when he realized that Akira accepted her as a lover and not him.

It's just that I don't think him actually raping Akira fits the narrative at all. One could say "well, Akira could have repressed those memories" - and, yes, sure. But c'mon, dude was raped by his brother, then raped by his wife? (that he probably married because their parents didn't accept him as homossexual?) (...)

And then we have an entire game based around him being robbed of his innocence by Sekai and making his entire life about that, when something just as tragic (or even more tbh) happened before it - and it doesn't affect him at all? (other than "I don't like pegging"?)
I really hope the Nozomu revelation doesn't go that way, although there has been some foreshadowing of that (especially during the last christmas update with the gnomes).

The poem in the background of the event
It wasn’t the bright hems of the Lord’s skirts
that brushed my face and I opened my eyes
to see from a cleft in rock His backside;

it’s a wasp perched on my left cheek. I keep
my eyes closed and stand perfectly still
in the garden till it leaves me alone,

not to contemplate how this century
ends and the next begins with no one
I know having seen God, but to wonder

why I get through most days unscathed, though I
live in a time when it might be otherwise,
and I grow more fatherless each day.

For years now I have come to conclusions
without my father’s help, discovering
on my own what I know, what I don’t know,

and seeing how one cancels the other.
I've become a scholar of cancellations.
Here, I stand among my father’s roses

and see that what punctures outnumbers what
consoles, the cruel and the tender never
make peace, though one climbs, though one descends

petal by petal to the hidden ground
no one owns. I see that which is taken
away by violence or persuasion.

The rose announces on earth the kingdom
of gravity. A bird cancels it.
My eyelids cancel the bird. Anything

might cancel my eyes: distance, time, war.
My father said, Never take your both eyes
off of the world, before he rocked me.

All night we waited for the knock
that would have signalled, All clear, come now;
it would have meant escape; it never came.

I didn’t make the world I leave you with,
he said, and then, being poor, he left me
only this world, in which there is always

a family waiting in terror
before they’re rended, this world wherein a man
might arise, go down, and walk along a path

and pause and bow to roses, roses
his father raised, and admire them, for one moment
unable, thank God, to see in each and
every flower the world cancelling itself.

Moonflare said:
this is a repeat of something I've said a few times, but I really hope it isn't revealed that Nozomu raped Akira.

I feel like it would really undermine what Sekai did, and make it kind of unrealistic that Akira even resented Nozomu for fucking/owning the woman he loved, when the act of having previously raped him would (imo) be of a much higher priority than that.

Now, if it is revealed that Nozomu wanted to rape Akira, that's fine. It's also something I've theorized about the possibility of him being jealous of Akira, rather than of Sekai in episodes like what Ami described about her scent. Maybe even to the possibility of Nozomu trying to kill her when he realized that Akira accepted her as a lover and not him.

It's just that I don't think him actually raping Akira fits the narrative at all. One could say "well, Akira could have repressed those memories" - and, yes, sure. But c'mon, dude was raped by his brother, then raped by his wife? (that he probably married because their parents didn't accept him as homossexual?) (...)

And then we have an entire game based around him being robbed of his innocence by Sekai and making his entire life about that, when something just as tragic (or even more tbh) happened before it - and it doesn't affect him at all? (other than "I don't like pegging"?)
I really hope the Nozomu revelation doesn't go that way, although there has been some foreshadowing of that (especially during the last christmas update with the gnomes).
Click to expand...
While i agree on it's impact on story with nozomu reveal, Happy event "Good Boy", talk about eating veggies and tying shoes correctly, makes the abuser an authority figure inside family.


Which means there are 4 suspects. Sekai (Good Boy makes it seem Sekai is an another abuser which groomes Akira to love her, while Akira is afraid and hate the other abuser) So there are 3:


-Yuu
-Nozomu
-Saki

About Yuu, we only have some flashbacks(?) about him that makes him some levelheaded, average hentai protagonist.

About Nozomu, in "S.omething E.veryone K.nows a.nd I.gnores", narrotor talks about someone who had a twisted idea of fun because he has to hides his sexuality. And the next happy event "Good Boy" we have a pov of someone who gets molested by a older family figure.

About Saki i have terrible memory so only thing i remember about her is:
- She is Akira's mother
- She didn't like Akira. (According to Yasu, in her knowledge battle against Rin)

And all there posibility decrease the impact of Sekai and worse, it sets the stage for revealing key details and introducing of new elements under the excuse that the Akira had forgotten them too.

But i think Selebus may make it work with making parallels with other characters.

Akira getting raped by Nozomu then groomed and raped by Sekai would explain relationship of Akira and Maya.

Both got molested at young age by some family figure. Both find a new older figure that still molest them, but under the guise of both broken people trying to mend each other with poem, philosophy and sex.

And i'm totally up for it. And prepares the purity route of Maya.

Basically Akira gets rid of Sekai's ghost/his love for her and same things happen with Maya who will stop loving Akira. Like i wrote in a earlier post, girls and Akira overcome their abusers by stop loving Akira/Sekai.
Which would be an amazing lesson in love.

Also I caught up with the pages, yayyyyyyyyy
About the Nozomu conversation I saw some pages ago:
I really hope he didn't rape Akira just as his wife did. I am for Akira being introduced to new traumas and experiences, but for his past to be even more tragic than it has been implied, feels very unnecessary. Maybe he was raped by a man, but it feels pointless and edgy for that man to have been his own brother.

I think at most he was physically abused by Nozomu. We all know Sekai sexually abused Akira (since he was in middle school? maybe even further back?), but there has also been hints of him suffering beatings since he was very young, we just don't know by whom, and why.

I do believe the most likely candidate to have physically abused Akira is his mother, Saki. Akira hated his brother, but he has nowhere near the same reaction towards Nozomu that he has towards Saki or Sekai. Perhaps Nozomu did hit him, but at the very least I do not think he was ever the biggest oppressor.

Maybe Akira's hatred for his brother was not just because he married and was loved by Sekai, but also because Nozomu too was loved by Saki.

A mother's love, something he never experienced from Saki, but that was freely given to Nozomu.
And then Sekai, who became Akira's mother figure, someone who showered him with "love". But even so, he couldn't help but think of himself as number 2.

A Mother's love, A Lover's love. Sekai was capable of providing both to Akira.
But everything changed with Ami's birth.

Where would have that left Akira at? Was there any space in Sekai's heart after Ami and Nozomu? Akira might doubt it.
After having a taste of what a mother's love is, how could he possibly go back to the times when he didn't receive it?

He had Niki, but it is not the same. Niki could never fulfill the role of nurture, protection, and warmth that he desired. At the very least, not the highschool Niki.

Where am I going with this? honestly not idea, I just wanted to write what I have thought.

posts.content_html_raw:
I read a conversation a couple of pages ago about the number of characters the game has, and it makes me wonder how the game story would've look like if Selebus stuck to the 10 original main cast plus fewer side characters.

It was a very important change that was very much at the discretion of the players, something Selebus rarely does when it comes to his "masterpiece". Like, he didn't even let us name Sensei whatever we wanted to. In hindsight it was a good decision considering how his name became a big reveal, but I remember back when the game launched some people were complaining about not being able to name him, but Selebus stood to his ground.

That is to say I can think of three separate reasons why Selebus decide to increase the cast size based on the players whims/support:

1. The story and characters were still loosely thought out back then, which is why Selebus had no issue adding more into the mix, and make it fit together as he went along.

2. He already planned the character cast to be as big as it is, but was VERY confident on his game success in patreon, so instead of simply introducing the new characters, he decided to dress it up as subscribers goals, knowing he would eventually reach them. Even if he didn't manage to reach the goals for all new characters, he could've still decided to add them into the game as an appreciate for the support. It is the same thing new multiplayer games do with pre-registration, it is a win-win either way.

3. Some of the backstory and plot events that was given to the new cast, was originally meant to be part of or happen with the First Floor + side characters, all Selebus did was dilute it into the new characters. Like imagine if some parts of Io's character story were meant to be for Yumi, or Nodoka for Ami. It might sound ridiculous and out of character right now because the characters are now "set in stone", but back then we still didn't know them well enough to make those assumptions, so Selebus could tweak them in whatever way he wanted to make it fit.

I think the real answer is probably a mix of the three. I can't imagine Sensei's past without Niki and Noriko existing. So at the very least they were always going to join the cast. Maybe Noriko didn't originally exist, so all Selebus did was simply divide the Niki character into two.

There are more similar things we can do, that would reduce the number of characters while still keeping the story mostly the same.

Of course right now it isn't something I would want, because I love the current cast we have. But I cannot be 100% confident in saying that the story would have been worse if it had fewer characters. At the very least, the update-to-update cycle would have been less excruciating if it didn't feel so bloated with character events. As some people have mentioned, there are characters who have gone a year without an event.

Actually now that I think about it, if second floor didn't exist, then that means Dorm Wars would also dissapear from the story.

hmmmm, does my hatred for Dorm Wars outweights my love for the second floor characters? not right now, but I will change my opinion if I have to suffer through the same shitty fucking Dorm Garbage Wars for 5 more years.

aramaug said:

Click to expand...
aramaug said:
When Chinami was very young she was able to get medical care thanks to an unnamed friend of Chiaki who pretended to be her mom. A while back, I speculated that the friend could have been Tsubasa. Thanks to new evidence, I now believe that theory is extremely likely to be true. [...]
Click to expand...
As for why she didn't help the Chosokabes after Chiaki's death, that hasn't been answered yet, but I will point out a few things:
1. This is a problem no matter who the friend is - even without Tsubasa's money a family friend could have given Chika a great deal of support after Chiaki's death, but for some reason she didn't.
2. We don't know Tsubasa wasn't helping them, only that she wasn't doing it openly. Tsubasa herself says that Chika is too proud to accept direct charity.
3. She didn't just disappear from their lives for a small number of years, she disappeared for some normal years plus countless years of resets. A lot could have changed in that time, especially since it seems like Tsubasa is aware of the resets (based on her conversation with Himawari).

I am currently almost at the end of the games available content and i have to say that these past few updates have been...unsatisfying.

I mean dont get me wrong we did get PLENTY of amazing moments sprinkled throughout.

Like for example when Icarus Nodoka got her wings melted.


Or the fact that Sel just outright confirmed the Organ theory
Or how he made Sekai seem more human
Or how he made Ami even crazier
Also the Monks and the upside house lore were nice,Tsubasa finally revealing her true self was wonderful.

But that is all.I find it so tragically funny that SO MANY THINGS are happening on my screen yet nothing is happening at the same time.I will give Sel some good faith though and say that Amis descend into madness is somewhat enjoyable and the seed he planted with Niki listening to Sekai will(probably) grown into a good enough tree but other than that? I am dissapointed.Most of the things that have happened is more so shock value with small crumbs of lore sprinkled throught and nothing else.I mean he wasted some potentially amazing moments like Tsuneyos and Imanis scenes just to further hammer down the point that Akira has given up.Truly a waste of potential if you ask me.


Anyways rant is over.Ill prolly finish everything in 2-3 days and then ill make one final post for my opinion on whatever content remains.I will keep following this game till its fated end but man these last few updates were dissapointing,and i hope Sel digs himself out of the hole he himself dug.Praise be!

PS:Would love to hear your guys opinion on this since im still pretty out of the loop.

posts.content_html_raw:
Hi guys. I heard you like charts! There are some co-occurence diagrams I made for LiL characters, based on wiki data. I'm not going to publish dataself itself, but there is a python script* in attached zip file in case you interested how I did it (actually I just asked AI to write a script)

* Do not execute scripts from unknown sources. For real, it's only here in case you want to read it


Character Co-occurrence Dendrograms - Algorithm Explanation

What are these plots?
These are "dendrograms" - tree-like diagrams that show how characters in a story are related to each other based on how often they appear together in events.

How do we measure character relationships?
We calculate "co-occurrence percentages" - how often each character appears in the same event as another character. For example:
- If Character A appears in 10 events total, and Character B appears in 8 of those same events, then B appears with A 80% of the time.

The algorithm step by step:

1. DATA PREPARATION
- Parsed wiki
- Extract which characters appear in each event. It was inaccurate but I don't care
- Remove the main character "Sensei" to focus on relationships between other characters

2. CO-OCCURRENCE CALCULATION
- For each pair of characters, count how many events they appear in together
- Convert to percentage: (shared events / total events for character A) × 100
- Create a matrix showing all character pairs and their co-occurrence percentages

3. DISTANCE CONVERSION
- Convert percentages to "distances" using the formula: distance = -log(percentage/100)
- This means: higher co-occurrence = lower distance (closer together)
- Characters that never appear together get maximum distance

4. HIERARCHICAL CLUSTERING
- Use "single linkage" clustering to group similar characters
- Start with each character as its own group
- Repeatedly merge the two closest groups until all characters are in one group
- The "single linkage" method uses the minimal distance between all pairs of characters from different groups

5. DENDROGRAM CREATION
- Draw a tree where:
* Character names are on the right side
* Horizontal lines show which characters are grouped together
* The x-axis shows co-occurrence percentage (higher percentage = closer to the right)
* Branch height shows how similar the groups are

What the results tell us:
- Characters close together on the right side appear together frequently
- Characters far apart rarely appear together
- Groups of characters that are clustered together have similar story patterns
- The height of branches shows how strong the relationships are

This helps visualize which characters form natural story groups or have similar narrative arcs!

- The "single linkage" method uses the minimal distance between all pairs of characters from different groups
5. DENDROGRAM CREATION
- Draw a tree where:
* Character names are on the right side
* Horizontal lines show which characters are grouped together
* The x-axis shows co-occurrence percentage (higher percentage = closer to the right)
* Branch height shows how similar the groups are
What the results tell us:
- Characters close together on the right side appear together frequently
- Characters far apart rarely appear together
- Groups of characters that are clustered together have similar story patterns
- The height of branches shows how strong the relationships are
This helps visualize which characters form natural story groups or have similar narrative arcs!

Billy becomes "unstuck in time" as a result of the psychological trauma he suffers. Clarifying/expanding on what fasoaga said: Billy Pilgrim is the protagonist of Kurt Vonnegut's Slaughterhouse-Five. After traumatic experiences as a POW in WWII he becomes "unstuck in time", which means he experiences moments from his life in an arbitrary, non-chronological order which he has no control over.

Sel has referenced this phrase before: in "Infinity House" the narrator described how people trapped there become "unstuck in eternity". As for Maya, she became unstuck in time during Halloween, living through moments from her past as if they were happening in the present. With an event title referencing that, I hope it means she's going to start telling Sensei about Halloween, though I'm sure she'll leave the Ami part out (the story won't allow him to learn about her yet).

My first thought with "A Second Haunting" is that it refers to Sekai's ghost (especially since she's in one of the Maya previews), in which case a second haunting could be Sensei seeing another ghost. Maybe there will just be multiple Sekais again, but the (very unrealistic) ideal scenario is that the ghost of Maya Prime shows up to snarkily comment on his passivity and indecision since her death.

My first thought with "A Second Haunting" is that it refers to Sekai's ghost (especially since she's in one of the Maya previews), in which case a second haunting could be Sensei seeing another ghost. Maybe there will just be multiple Sekais again, but the (very unrealistic) ideal scenario is that the ghost of Maya Prime shows up to snarkily comment on his passivity and indecision since her death.

How do you imagine a purity route if it's going to end up being reset? that's sad and not the way it will happen.

Here's a question for you.
If you've lived a life and suddenly you were to forget everything, is the old you dead and you are now a different person, or is it still you?

You have already seen it before, different Senseis who are different from each other but originated from the same vantage point somewhere in the past. One likes poetry, another likes football, another is a remorseless groomer, all of them shaped by circumstance, and are so different that you can't call them the same person anymore.

I've already said it before, but our current Akira is the chosen one, I think he has inside of him the memories of previous Akiras that were reset but never deleted.
When you start a new game of LiL, everyone forgets everything, but your save file is still there and you can make them remember if you chose to by loading it.

Scientifically, if has been proven that a person can be romantically "in-love" with two people at the same time, but in our story, there have been so many endless resets that he has fallen in love with every single girl at some point in the past, it's all just locked inside until he remembers again.
So when Akira says "I love you" to a girl, he really feels it, because it has happened, he just doesn't remember, and the girls are the same too.

All of this amounts to Akira being one and everyone of himself at the same time. Now I don't know how Selebus will choose to do it (I have some ideas of my own), but you can easily get every purity route, harem and True endings to be cannon at the same time, if you can just SPLIT YOUR SOUL.

posts.content_html_raw:
I wrote a lot but decided to save it for another time, because I was starting to get on a rambling groove, so I need more time to let the theory simmer.

But the beginning of it is:

If you had the choice, would you willingly leave the Kumon-Mi and the resets? assuming that you have Sensei's and Rooftop Apocalypse Squad's ability of keeping your memories.
I'm not sure if I could make that choice.

When it comes to timeloops scenarios, the one in LiL is kinda amazing compared to other timeloops I have read about. Not having to worry about my ever-approaching doom and withering of my physical body? The timeloop period is every 6-ish months? It comes with a change of seasons? A whole city full of activities? And assuming you have Sensei's special ability of working as an anchor for everyone's memories, so you also get to carry with you the connections you made each reset? I get to experience lifetimes of suffering and happiness.

I don't even have to worry about living an immortal life. I can just let myself be reseted. Losing all your memories is no different from dying.

So, would you be willing to leave all of that behind for the outside world? A world that probably would not be different to the one inside Kumon-Mi, except that you get to wither and die?

As I mentioned, if there was a tierlist of timeloops, LiL's would be an S-Tier one. That is of course, if we ignore the ever increasing corruption of this world, its possibly close end, and the way it might try to fight against it...

This is when I went off the rails and started rambling, so that's it for now

posts.content_html_raw:
random thought regarding the purity routes
Selebus said that it's going to be in a vn form, and I hope that he utilizes fake choices in that vn as well. What I mean is that during the course of the main game we often find ourselves pissed at Akira for his inaction. I think it would be cathartic to not only see him taking action, but to actually choose to take that action ourselves.

Think about it like a newgame+ situation, where in the first timeline you had no other choice (like in the Yumi assault situation at the beginning of the game), but then during the "second timeline/newgame+/purity route" you now have that choice. How rewarding would it be for the player to pick the choice themselves?

There are many vns that implement such a system, for instance, the routes in fate/stay night only unlock after you play through the previous ones. And the way you enter them is by playing the game and choosing new choices (previously unavailable). We're still many years away from them, but it would be interesting.
Although, granted, to have LiL as a book is what I've been asking from the start - so it's a win/win to me, choice or no choice.

posts.content_html_raw:
I know there has been a lot of discussion on red/green routes in the past, but one I never see mentioned is telling Karin about Akira's relationship with her sister.

Lying to Karin and saying you are not involved If you don't lie, it causes you to miss 'Dying alone with ten cats'. Which is a fun event.

But telling Karin that you have been with her sister; it really changes her attitude. It really brings out the competitive/rivalry side of Karin. It feels like it fits with the rest of the story better (granted, I'm only at 'Wrong Place/Wrong Time' in my 2nd playthrough, so there could be more changes I am not aware of)

Anyone else find this? Is the missed event worth it to see this side of Karin? Or is the 'green' version of Karin the best?

In anticipation of the big revelations we're about to get about Sara's past (Selebus please), let's talk about the identity of her teacher, i.e. Sana's dad. I think Nozomu Arakawa is the most likely candidate, but I'm far from certain. What I am confident in: Sana is an Arakawa.

(OK, the day before an update probably isn't the best time for a long theory post, but I was determined to share what I have before we get The Sara Update. Nakayamas? Never heard of 'em. I would have posted last week but circumstances prevented it.)

I'm going to start from the idea that Sana's dad and Rin's mysterious bio dad are the same person (but even if that turns out to be wrong, much of the evidence still applies to Sana's dad). For details, see this post:
aramaug said:
I believe that Sana and Rin are half-sisters who the share the same biological dad.
[...]
Click to expand...
I tried structuring things a bit differently this time, splitting into subsections and in particular separating most of the screenshot evidence (first two sections) from the analysis/thesis. Let me know if this is helpful or just makes things harder to follow.
Note: I'm not saying any of these points are definitively foreshadowing in isolation. But they all give circumstantial evidence pointing in the same direction.

1. Akira has nieces who aren't Ami.
Akira is going to swap Ami for a different niece. Half of this has come true: Ami is now his daughter.


He has "hidden" family members that probably include nieces, plural.
2. Sana is related to the Arakawas.
Sana will "suddenly" become related to Ami and Akira. In theory this happens if Akira marries Sara, but it's very carefully worded so that it's consistent with revealing an existing relationship instead.

Akira is already basically family.

...
3. Akira is like a father to Sana and in particular has many similarities with her real dad.


...

And the strongest evidence of all:

It's like the old saying goes, all brothers headpat alike.
4. Akira is like a father to Rin... or an uncle?

posts.content_html_raw:
aramaug said:
[snip]
Click to expand...
Sana and Rin's father, continued.
1. Sara has gone through periods of the gods messing with her mind, and these seem to coincide with her two relationships.

She associates her "curse" with her time in high school, i.e. the period of her relationship with Sana's father.


Although she's been keeping it a secret, recently her issues have started again. Possibly this coincides with the start of her new relationship with Sensei.

Translation: "why does everything have to hurt so much" (Vigenere cipher with key "XXX")

"WHY NOW?! THIS IS SUPPOSED TO BE OVER!" (redacted dialog given in script comment)
2. The gods "know" Sara from her past and supposedly fathered Sana.
She's one of Pareidolia's favorites and he associates her with someone Sensei never met, implying he already knew Sara from before.

Pegasus identifies himself as Sana's father, linking him somehow to Sara's teacher.
3. Sana and Rin are both "chosen" by god(s).
Like Sensei and unlike the other girls, they're allowed into Yasu's church. I think Pareidolia is the one who chose them since this happens in Chapter 3 when he's taken over Yasu's church.
4. I suspect the gods drove Rin's bio mom insane.
Along with Sara, Pareidolia has a second favorite who Sensei doesn't know. It makes a lot of sense for this to be Rin's bio mom: she's an important character Sensei hasn't met, she's tied to Sara through their shared baby daddy, and their children were both chosen by (probably) Pareidolia.

Rin's mom is described as psycho and virtually mute, which sounds like one of Sensei's blackouts.

...

Sara experienced similar symptoms during high school, but was able to overcome them and avoid going insane. In particular she risked becoming "lost inside of herself" like a mute crazy person might.

I think Rin's mom had the same curse, but wasn't so lucky; she couldn't overcome it and instead went insane.
5. The simplest way to explain all of these points is that Sara's teacher is the cause of the godfuckery.
Maybe Pegasus just happened to cuck Sara's teacher at the right moment to be the actual father of Sana. Maybe Rin's mother is just regular crazy and has no actual connection to the gods. Maybe Sara and Rin's mom just happen to share symptoms and also just happen to have been groomed by the same man. In isolation, each of these could be explained as just coincidence (though you have to question why Sel would choose to write it that way), but when considered together the series of coincidences becomes increasingly improbable.

In contrast, everything can be explained by a simple theory: Sara's teacher was "chosen" by Pareidolia, who was in his head and experienced his sexual conquests. He transmitted a supernatural curse to the people he was in relationships with. His children inherited his chosen status from him.
I'm not going to try to justify these in this post, but I have two theories regarding Pegasus that I go back and forth on:
  • Pegasus and Pareidolia are different identities assumed by the same entity (USER3).
  • Pegasus is the "ghost" of Sana's father, who struck a deal with Pareidolia.
It's even possible they both contain an element of truth. Either way I think Pegasus's claims are consistent with Sana having a human father who had Pareidolia in his head.
6. Sekai might have experienced a curse similar to Sara and Rin's mom.
Toward the end of her life, she was hearing voices and going mad. Pareidolia specifically calls it an infection.

And Pareidolia doesn't only talk about her like he was in her head; he also lusts after her like she's another of his "favorites".

I don't want to draw too many conclusions from this. As Yuu's daughter, Sekai probably had a hereditary connection to the gods. Even if her curse was exacerbated by a relationship, it could have been because of Akira, who presumably had Pareidolia in his head even then. But I can't help but think that the way Pareidolia objectifies her is more likely to come from Nozomu.
1. Sana and Rin's dad is someone important to the story beyond just linking the two of them.
- He likely has an importance to the supernatural plot, based on the connection the Sakakibaras share with Rin and her mom.

- He likely has a connection to Sensei's past: He taught at Sara's high school, which from "Good Boy" is the abandoned school that keeps showing up in happy events and so must have some importance in Sensei's subconscious.

- His name is being hidden from us (and Sensei): With how much we've learned about this guy, his name should have come up at some point, similar to other off screen characters like Masahiro, Tomonori, Rie, etc. This is especially true since Sara wants to track him down and make him pay child support - she should be naming and shaming him in hopes that anyone has heard about his current whereabouts. Most likely we haven't learned the name because it would reveal something that it's too early for us to know. (Possible counterexample: I doubt the name of Haruka's husband has any importance, but he's never been referred to by name in conversations where it would be natural to do so.)

- Something needs to give his reveal impact: Finding out that Sana and Rin are sisters will be momentarily surprising, but it's not going to cause a significant change in their relationship or really affect the story. It has to come with some shocking revelation about their father in order to feel like an important twist.

- The reveal needs to happen somehow: Nobody knows who Rin's dad was except for her insane mom. Nobody knows which other girls Sara's teacher was seeing. I don't see how we get the reveal that they're the same person unless someone else (could be a god) knew the guy for a different reason. He's likely dead now (see below), in which case he can't show up to make the reveal himself.
In light of all that, I don't give serious consideration to the idea that their dad is some rando or someone who hasn't been introduced to the story at all yet.

2. Things we know about Sana's dad exclude almost all known characters.
  1. He was a high school teacher approximately fifteen years ago, which probably excludes people with known professions like Tomonori, Mr. Tojo, and Takoyaki Man.
  2. He was significantly older than Sara, which excludes a lot of random very important side characters, such as Frank: Friend of Tony: Takoyaki Son, Son of Takoyaki Man.
  3. He was a serial cheater who groomed multiple young girls while tricking Sara into thinking he was a great guy, which I think probably excludes Yuu, who consistently comes across as kind but lazy in his own thoughts (including in NiB).
  4. He's probably dead and has no living children beyond Sana and Rin, which obviously excludes all the other girls' dads. I'm basing this off the throwaway line from sports wars that Sana was "survived by" Sara and "one other", who I assume is Rin. I think this line should be taken literally - Sel had to know it would be interpreted as foreshadowing, especially when the mystery of Sana's family is clearly important, and I don't think he would put in foreshadowing that's just false.
3. All of these things could be true of Nozomu.
  1. There's no direct evidence that Nozomu was a teacher, but his brother, half-sister/wife, and probably mother all were, so it's a common occupation in his family. Nozomu's wife also probably taught at the same school.
  2. We don't know Nozomu's exact age, but he was old enough to be in a legitimate relationship with Sekai when Akira was still quite young.
  3. Nozomu beat his wife, possibly abused his young brother, and generally comes across as an unpleasant person. He apparently managed to keep this all hidden from his own daughter: Ami says his biggest fault was that he was too normal.
  4. Nozomu is dead and has no known living children, assuming that Akira is Ami's biological father. Sana is survived by Sara and Rin, with Akira and Ami not included because they're extended family (uncle and cousin) rather than immediate.
This is by no means compelling, but it's at least plausible, which is more than we can say for other candidates.
4. Nozomu fits the foreshadowing very well.
  • If Sensei has secret nieces, they're probably Nozomu's children, and if Nozomu has children, Sana and Rin are by far the most likely given the mystery surrounding their father.
  • Sana would already be related to the Arakawas through her dad.
  • Sensei is being compared to Sana's real dad because they would have been brothers.
  • Sensei is a father figure (but really an uncle) to Sana and Rin because he would be their only living adult male family member.
5. Nozomu fits the connection to the gods very well.
For one thing, he supposedly shares his name with one of the gods (worth noting: the only characters who have ever referred to USER1 as Nozomu are Pareidolia and a couple of shady narrators), though I don't want to identify the two Nozomus as the same entity or anything.

More importantly, connection to the gods and especially Pareidolia seems to run in the Arakawa family. Sensei has Pareidolia in his head. Sekai and Yuu both heard the voice of god(s), and Pareidolia talks like he knew them the same way he knows Sensei. After Sekai's death, her ghost is working for/with Pareidolia and her organs let Pareidolia control Kaori. Ami talks to voices and has an "infection" that almost certainly invovles Pareidolia. Even Nodoka seems to be influenced by Sekai and Pareidolia, although it isn't clear whether they actually speak to her directly.

Yumi seems to be the exception that shows you don't need to be an Arakawa (barring tinfoil theories) to have Pareidolia in your head, but the Pareidolia infection does seem to be hereditary. And given that all of Nozomu's immediate family were infected, it's pretty likely he was as well and could pass this infection on to his own children. Nozomu being Sana's father thus gives us a clean explanation for why both of them are connected to Pareidolia.

This also links Sekai with Sara and Rin's mom because all three were sexual partners of Nozomu, which could explain her infection as another instance of Sara's curse. Note also that Sara's issues have started again while she's (for a second time?) in a relationship with an Arakawa.
There are two things we know about Nozomu that Sara should have known had he been her teacher, but which don't seem to be consistent with what she has and hasn't said:
  1. Nozomu was married, but Sara thought she was in a dedicated monogamous relationship with her teacher.
  2. Nozomu's surname was Arakawa, but Sara hasn't noticed that Sensei has the same surname as her teacher.
Possible explanations and why I find them unsatisfactory:
- Sara isn't telling the full truth, either because the gods forced her to forget things or because she's lying to herself.
I don't know of any direct evidence for either of these possibilities. In any case, Haruka went to the same school and almost certainly knew who Sara's teacher was. She has no reason to lie about it, and there's no indication the gods messed with her.

- (For #1 only) Nozomu and Sekai weren't married yet or the marriage was a secret, possibly because they knew they were related.
The evidence doesn't back this up: the Xoanon says "your brother's wife" took care of wizard Akira, and Mrs. Nakayama refers to Sekai as Akira's sister-in-law in "Kyoto".

- Timeline shenanigans, for example Sara comes from a world where Nozomu and Sekai never got married.
There's no real evidence for this and it opens up a can of worms about how Sana and Ami can exist in the same timeline, especially when plenty of people remember each of them from well before the resets.

- (For #2 only) Sara doesn't know that Sensei's surname is Arakawa.
I was convinced by this one for a little while: Sara has never said the name Arakawa, and i don't think anyone has ever used it in direct conversation with her. Same is true for Haruka, who should also recognize the name of Sara's teacher. However, I found one case where Imani says it while Sara is present and implied to be paying attention.
In theory Sara could be too distracted to notice, but I can't see Selebus intentionally putting this in the game if he's intending a later reveal where Sara reacts to the name Arakawa.
Theory #1: Yuu was Sara's teacher and the father of Sana and Rin.
Advantages:
  • Yuu probably abandoned his family with Saki, so he wouldn't be married and might have used an assumed name so that they couldn't track him down.
  • We know for sure that Yuu had a supernatural connection and was much older than Sara, whereas we're only guessing for Nozomu.
  • Many of the clues only point toward Sana's dad being an Arakawa, which obviously fits Yuu just as much as Nozomu.
Problems:
  • Sana would have at least two living siblings (Akira and Rin), so the "survived by one other" line can't be taken literally.
  • Sara's teacher (manipulative, sexual predator, prone to anger) had a drastically different personality from young Yuu (kind, lazy).
  • Sana and Rin would be Akira's half-sisters instead of his nieces, so the foreshadowing of secret nieces would need to be explained elsewhere.
  • Pareidolia says that nobody remembers Yuu, as if all memories of his existence were erased from the terminal. While Sara might have forgotten some things, she certainly remembers far more about her teacher than Sensei does about his father.
I find this theory plausible, but I think the problems are harder to overcome than for the Nozomu theory.

Theory #2: Sara is Yuu's daughter.
There are three girls in the NiB demo: Saki, Miu, and Reina. LiL has characters that are Yuu's children with Saki (Nozomu, Akira) and with Miu (Sekai). If he also had a child with Reina, Sara is the most likely candidate as they both have dark hair and green eyes.

Advantages:
  • Explains the foreshadowing that the Arakawas and Sakakibaras are related.
  • Explains Sara's (and Sana's) supernatural connection as coming from her parents rather than her teacher.
  • Explains one secret niece (Sana), though not why Ami refers to nieces, plural.
Problems:
  • The father who raised Sara can't be Yuu - his surname and personality don't fit and he owned the bar even before Sara was born, meaning before Akira was conceived. There's no hint she's adopted - if she is I would have expected her emotionally abusive parents to rub it in her face at every opportunity.
  • The identity of Sana's father is still a mystery, especially if he also fathered Rin. Doesn't explain the foreshadowing linking him to Sensei.
  • Rin's chosen status and her mother's madness aren't explained.
I find this theory unlikely but not impossible. It's also not mutually exclusive with the theories about Sara's teacher; after all, the Arakawas are the incest family.

Theory #3: Sana secretly isn't the daughter of Sara's teacher, but rather of Sara's younger classmate Akira Arakawa.
The idea is that in her senior year Sara "cheated" on her teacher with freshman Akira, then the gods forced both of them to forget.

Advantages:
  • There are some hints that there might have been a timeline where Sara and Akira actually knew each other in high school.
  • Explains the foreshadowing that Sensei is like Sana's dad because he actually is her real dad (though this gets murky when they're really talking about similarities between Sensei and Sara's teacher).
Problems:
  • Leaves pretty much everything else unexplained: Sara's teacher (who would still have to be Shota's dad), Rin's parents, Sensei's nieces, etc.
  • Like with Yuu, we'd have to dismiss that Sana is "survived by one other" since Akira and Rin would both be members of her immediate family.
I don't consider this a serious possibility, I'm just including it for completeness.

Theory #4: Adult Akira was Sara's teacher thanks to alternate timelines, time travel, or some other such bullshit.
I think this one can be rejected pretty quickly: the teen Sara in "Good Boy" has a boyfriend (her teacher), but doesn't recognize Sensei at all.
TLDR: Lots of little hints can be explained if Nozomu was the father of Sana and Rin. On the other hand, parts of Sara's story about her teacher seem to be inconsistent with Nozomu. But since I find all other alternatives even less likely, I lean toward the belief that Nozomu is the father and Sara's omissions will be explained in a way that we don't yet understand.

2. The gods "know" Sara from her past and supposedly fathered Sana.
Spoiler
She's one of Pareidolia's favorites and he associates her with someone Sensei never met, implying he already knew Sara from before.
Pegasus identifies himself as Sana's father, linking him somehow to Sara's teacher.
3. Sana and Rin are both "chosen" by god(s).
Spoiler
Like Sensei and unlike the other girls, they're allowed into Yasu's church. I think Pareidolia is the one who chose them since this happens in Chapter 3 when he's taken over Yasu's church.
4. I suspect the gods drove Rin's bio mom insane.
Spoiler
Along with Sara, Pareidolia has a second favorite who Sensei doesn't know. It makes a lot of sense for this to be Rin's bio mom: she's an important character Sensei hasn't met, she's tied to Sara through their shared baby daddy, and their children were both chosen by (probably) Pareidolia.
Rin's mom is described as psycho and virtually mute, which sounds like one of Sensei's blackouts.
...
Sara experienced similar symptoms during high school, but was able to overcome them and avoid going insane. In particular she risked becoming "lost inside of herself" like a mute crazy person might.
I think Rin's mom had the same curse, but wasn't so lucky; she couldn't overcome it and instead went insane.
5. The simplest way to explain all of these points is that Sara's teacher is the cause of the godfuckery.
Spoiler
Maybe Pegasus just happened to cuck Sara's teacher at the right moment to be the actual father of Sana. Maybe Rin's mother is just regular crazy and has no actual connection to the gods. Maybe Sara and Rin's mom just happen to share symptoms and also just happen to have been groomed by the same man. In isolation, each of these could be explained as just coincidence (though you have to question why Sel would choose to write it that way), but when considered together the series of coincidences becomes increasingly improbable.
In contrast, everything can be explained by a simple theory: Sara's teacher was "chosen" by Pareidolia, who was in his head and experienced his sexual conquests. He transmitted a supernatural curse to the people he was in relationships with. His children inherited his chosen status from him.

might
have experienced a curse similar to Sara and Rin's mom.

spoilers.title: 3. The case for Nozomu Arakawa
spoilers.html:
1. Sana and Rin's dad is someone important to the story beyond just linking the two of them.
- He likely has an importance to the supernatural plot, based on the connection the Sakakibaras share with Rin and her mom.

- He likely has a connection to Sensei's past: He taught at Sara's high school, which from "Good Boy" is the abandoned school that keeps showing up in happy events and so must have some importance in Sensei's subconscious.

- His name is being hidden from us (and Sensei): With how much we've learned about this guy, his name should have come up at some point, similar to other off screen characters like Masahiro, Tomonori, Rie, etc. This is especially true since Sara wants to track him down and make him pay child support - she should be naming and shaming him in hopes that anyone has heard about his current whereabouts. Most likely we haven't learned the name because it would reveal something that it's too early for us to know. (Possible counterexample: I doubt the name of Haruka's husband has any importance, but he's never been referred to by name in conversations where it would be natural to do so.)

- Something needs to give his reveal impact: Finding out that Sana and Rin are sisters will be momentarily surprising, but it's not going to cause a significant change in their relationship or really affect the story. It has to come with some shocking revelation about their father in order to feel like an important twist.

- The reveal needs to happen somehow: Nobody knows who Rin's dad was except for her insane mom. Nobody knows which other girls Sara's teacher was seeing. I don't see how we get the reveal that they're the same person unless someone else (could be a god) knew the guy for a different reason. He's likely dead now (see below), in which case he can't show up to make the reveal himself.
In light of all that, I don't give serious consideration to the idea that their dad is some rando or someone who hasn't been introduced to the story at all yet.

2. Things we know about Sana's dad exclude almost all known characters.
  1. He was a high school teacher approximately fifteen years ago, which probably excludes people with known professions like Tomonori, Mr. Tojo, and Takoyaki Man.
  2. He was significantly older than Sara, which excludes a lot of random very important side characters, such as Frank: Friend of Tony: Takoyaki Son, Son of Takoyaki Man.
  3. He was a serial cheater who groomed multiple young girls while tricking Sara into thinking he was a great guy, which I think probably excludes Yuu, who consistently comes across as kind but lazy in his own thoughts (including in NiB).
  4. He's probably dead and has no living children beyond Sana and Rin, which obviously excludes all the other girls' dads. I'm basing this off the throwaway line from sports wars that Sana was "survived by" Sara and "one other", who I assume is Rin. I think this line should be taken literally - Sel had to know it would be interpreted as foreshadowing, especially when the mystery of Sana's family is clearly important, and I don't think he would put in foreshadowing that's just false.
3. All of these things could be true of Nozomu.
  1. There's no direct evidence that Nozomu was a teacher, but his brother, half-sister/wife, and probably mother all were, so it's a common occupation in his family. Nozomu's wife also probably taught at the same school.
  2. We don't know Nozomu's exact age, but he was old enough to be in a legitimate relationship with Sekai when Akira was still quite young.
  3. Nozomu beat his wife, possibly abused his young brother, and generally comes across as an unpleasant person. He apparently managed to keep this all hidden from his own daughter: Ami says his biggest fault was that he was too normal.
  4. Nozomu is dead and has no known living children, assuming that Akira is Ami's biological father. Sana is survived by Sara and Rin, with Akira and Ami not included because they're extended family (uncle and cousin) rather than immediate.
This is by no means compelling, but it's at least plausible, which is more than we can say for other candidates.
4. Nozomu fits the foreshadowing very well.
  • If Sensei has secret nieces, they're probably Nozomu's children, and if Nozomu has children, Sana and Rin are by far the most likely given the mystery surrounding their father.
  • Sana would already be related to the Arakawas through her dad.
  • Sensei is being compared to Sana's real dad because they would have been brothers.
  • Sensei is a father figure (but really an uncle) to Sana and Rin because he would be their only living adult male family member.
5. Nozomu fits the connection to the gods very well.
For one thing, he supposedly shares his name with one of the gods (worth noting: the only characters who have ever referred to USER1 as Nozomu are Pareidolia and a couple of shady narrators), though I don't want to identify the two Nozomus as the same entity or anything.

More importantly, connection to the gods and especially Pareidolia seems to run in the Arakawa family. Sensei has Pareidolia in his head. Sekai and Yuu both heard the voice of god(s), and Pareidolia talks like he knew them the same way he knows Sensei. After Sekai's death, her ghost is working for/with Pareidolia and her organs let Pareidolia control Kaori. Ami talks to voices and has an "infection" that almost certainly invovles Pareidolia. Even Nodoka seems to be influenced by Sekai and Pareidolia, although it isn't clear whether they actually speak to her directly.

Yumi seems to be the exception that shows you don't need to be an Arakawa (barring tinfoil theories) to have Pareidolia in your head, but the Pareidolia infection does seem to be hereditary. And given that all of Nozomu's immediate family were infected, it's pretty likely he was as well and could pass this infection on to his own children. Nozomu being Sana's father thus gives us a clean explanation for why both of them are connected to Pareidolia.

This also links Sekai with Sara and Rin's mom because all three were sexual partners of Nozomu, which could explain her infection as another instance of Sara's curse. Note also that Sara's issues have started again while she's (for a second time?) in a relationship with an Arakawa.

For one thing, he supposedly shares his name with one of the gods (worth noting: the only characters who have ever referred to USER1 as Nozomu are Pareidolia and a couple of shady narrators), though I don't want to identify the two Nozomus as the same entity or anything.

More importantly, connection to the gods and especially Pareidolia seems to run in the Arakawa family. Sensei has Pareidolia in his head. Sekai and Yuu both heard the voice of god(s), and Pareidolia talks like he knew them the same way he knows Sensei. After Sekai's death, her ghost is working for/with Pareidolia and her organs let Pareidolia control Kaori. Ami talks to voices and has an "infection" that almost certainly invovles Pareidolia. Even Nodoka seems to be influenced by Sekai and Pareidolia, although it isn't clear whether they actually speak to her directly.

Yumi seems to be the exception that shows you don't need to be an Arakawa (barring tinfoil theories) to have Pareidolia in your head, but the Pareidolia infection does seem to be hereditary. And given that all of Nozomu's immediate family were infected, it's pretty likely he was as well and could pass this infection on to his own children. Nozomu being Sana's father thus gives us a clean explanation for why both of them are connected to Pareidolia.

This also links Sekai with Sara and Rin's mom because all three were sexual partners of Nozomu, which could explain her infection as another instance of Sara's curse. Note also that Sara's issues have started again while she's (for a second time?) in a relationship with an Arakawa.

spoilers.title: 4. Problems with the Nozomu theory
spoilers.html:
There are two things we know about Nozomu that Sara should have known had he been her teacher, but which don't seem to be consistent with what she has and hasn't said:
  1. Nozomu was married, but Sara thought she was in a dedicated monogamous relationship with her teacher.
  2. Nozomu's surname was Arakawa, but Sara hasn't noticed that Sensei has the same surname as her teacher.
Possible explanations and why I find them unsatisfactory:
- Sara isn't telling the full truth, either because the gods forced her to forget things or because she's lying to herself.
I don't know of any direct evidence for either of these possibilities. In any case, Haruka went to the same school and almost certainly knew who Sara's teacher was. She has no reason to lie about it, and there's no indication the gods messed with her.

- (For #1 only) Nozomu and Sekai weren't married yet or the marriage was a secret, possibly because they knew they were related.
The evidence doesn't back this up: the Xoanon says "your brother's wife" took care of wizard Akira, and Mrs. Nakayama refers to Sekai as Akira's sister-in-law in "Kyoto".

- Timeline shenanigans, for example Sara comes from a world where Nozomu and Sekai never got married.
There's no real evidence for this and it opens up a can of worms about how Sana and Ami can exist in the same timeline, especially when plenty of people remember each of them from well before the resets.

- (For #2 only) Sara doesn't know that Sensei's surname is Arakawa.
I was convinced by this one for a little while: Sara has never said the name Arakawa, and i don't think anyone has ever used it in direct conversation with her. Same is true for Haruka, who should also recognize the name of Sara's teacher. However, I found one case where Imani says it while Sara is present and implied to be paying attention.
In theory Sara could be too distracted to notice, but I can't see Selebus intentionally putting this in the game if he's intending a later reveal where Sara reacts to the name Arakawa.

spoilers.title: 5. Alternate Theories
spoilers.html:
Theory #1: Yuu was Sara's teacher and the father of Sana and Rin.
Advantages:
  • Yuu probably abandoned his family with Saki, so he wouldn't be married and might have used an assumed name so that they couldn't track him down.
  • We know for sure that Yuu had a supernatural connection and was much older than Sara, whereas we're only guessing for Nozomu.
  • Many of the clues only point toward Sana's dad being an Arakawa, which obviously fits Yuu just as much as Nozomu.
Problems:
  • Sana would have at least two living siblings (Akira and Rin), so the "survived by one other" line can't be taken literally.
  • Sara's teacher (manipulative, sexual predator, prone to anger) had a drastically different personality from young Yuu (kind, lazy).
  • Sana and Rin would be Akira's half-sisters instead of his nieces, so the foreshadowing of secret nieces would need to be explained elsewhere.
  • Pareidolia says that nobody remembers Yuu, as if all memories of his existence were erased from the terminal. While Sara might have forgotten some things, she certainly remembers far more about her teacher than Sensei does about his father.
I find this theory plausible, but I think the problems are harder to overcome than for the Nozomu theory.

Theory #2: Sara is Yuu's daughter.
There are three girls in the NiB demo: Saki, Miu, and Reina. LiL has characters that are Yuu's children with Saki (Nozomu, Akira) and with Miu (Sekai). If he also had a child with Reina, Sara is the most likely candidate as they both have dark hair and green eyes.

Advantages:
  • Explains the foreshadowing that the Arakawas and Sakakibaras are related.
  • Explains Sara's (and Sana's) supernatural connection as coming from her parents rather than her teacher.
  • Explains one secret niece (Sana), though not why Ami refers to nieces, plural.
Problems:
  • The father who raised Sara can't be Yuu - his surname and personality don't fit and he owned the bar even before Sara was born, meaning before Akira was conceived. There's no hint she's adopted - if she is I would have expected her emotionally abusive parents to rub it in her face at every opportunity.
  • The identity of Sana's father is still a mystery, especially if he also fathered Rin. Doesn't explain the foreshadowing linking him to Sensei.
  • Rin's chosen status and her mother's madness aren't explained.
I find this theory unlikely but not impossible. It's also not mutually exclusive with the theories about Sara's teacher; after all, the Arakawas are the incest family.

Theory #3: Sana secretly isn't the daughter of Sara's teacher, but rather of Sara's younger classmate Akira Arakawa.
The idea is that in her senior year Sara "cheated" on her teacher with freshman Akira, then the gods forced both of them to forget.

Advantages:
  • There are some hints that there might have been a timeline where Sara and Akira actually knew each other in high school.
  • Explains the foreshadowing that Sensei is like Sana's dad because he actually is her real dad (though this gets murky when they're really talking about similarities between Sensei and Sara's teacher).
Problems:
  • Leaves pretty much everything else unexplained: Sara's teacher (who would still have to be Shota's dad), Rin's parents, Sensei's nieces, etc.
  • Like with Yuu, we'd have to dismiss that Sana is "survived by one other" since Akira and Rin would both be members of her immediate family.
I don't consider this a serious possibility, I'm just including it for completeness.

Theory #4: Adult Akira was Sara's teacher thanks to alternate timelines, time travel, or some other such bullshit.
I think this one can be rejected pretty quickly: the teen Sara in "Good Boy" has a boyfriend (her teacher), but doesn't recognize Sensei at all.

View attachment 4997732 View attachment 4997734
I don't want to draw too many conclusions from this. As Yuu's daughter, Sekai probably had a hereditary connection to the gods. Even if her curse was exacerbated by a relationship, it could have been because of Akira, who presumably had Pareidolia in his head even then. But I can't help but think that the way Pareidolia objectifies her is more likely to come from Nozomu.
1. Sana and Rin's dad is someone important to the story beyond just linking the two of them.
- He likely has an importance to the supernatural plot, based on the connection the Sakakibaras share with Rin and her mom.

- He likely has a connection to Sensei's past: He taught at Sara's high school, which from "Good Boy" is the abandoned school that keeps showing up in happy events and so must have some importance in Sensei's subconscious.

- His name is being hidden from us (and Sensei): With how much we've learned about this guy, his name should have come up at some point, similar to other off screen characters like Masahiro, Tomonori, Rie, etc. This is especially true since Sara wants to track him down and make him pay child support - she should be naming and shaming him in hopes that anyone has heard about his current whereabouts. Most likely we haven't learned the name because it would reveal something that it's too early for us to know. (Possible counterexample: I doubt the name of Haruka's husband has any importance, but he's never been referred to by name in conversations where it would be natural to do so.)

- Something needs to give his reveal impact: Finding out that Sana and Rin are sisters will be momentarily surprising, but it's not going to cause a significant change in their relationship or really affect the story. It has to come with some shocking revelation about their father in order to feel like an important twist.

- The reveal needs to happen somehow: Nobody knows who Rin's dad was except for her insane mom. Nobody knows which other girls Sara's teacher was seeing. I don't see how we get the reveal that they're the same person unless someone else (could be a god) knew the guy for a different reason. He's likely dead now (see below), in which case he can't show up to make the reveal himself.
In light of all that, I don't give serious consideration to the idea that their dad is some rando or someone who hasn't been introduced to the story at all yet.

2. Things we know about Sana's dad exclude almost all known characters.
  1. He was a high school teacher approximately fifteen years ago, which probably excludes people with known professions like Tomonori, Mr. Tojo, and Takoyaki Man.
  2. He was significantly older than Sara, which excludes a lot of random very important side characters, such as Frank: Friend of Tony: Takoyaki Son, Son of Takoyaki Man.
  3. He was a serial cheater who groomed multiple young girls while tricking Sara into thinking he was a great guy, which I think probably excludes Yuu, who consistently comes across as kind but lazy in his own thoughts (including in NiB).
  4. He's probably dead and has no living children beyond Sana and Rin, which obviously excludes all the other girls' dads. I'm basing this off the throwaway line from sports wars that Sana was "survived by" Sara and "one other", who I assume is Rin. I think this line should be taken literally - Sel had to know it would be interpreted as foreshadowing, especially when the mystery of Sana's family is clearly important, and I don't think he would put in foreshadowing that's just false.
    View attachment 4997754 View attachment 4997755
3. All of these things could be true of Nozomu.
  1. There's no direct evidence that Nozomu was a teacher, but his brother, half-sister/wife, and probably mother all were, so it's a common occupation in his family. Nozomu's wife also probably taught at the same school.
  2. We don't know Nozomu's exact age, but he was old enough to be in a legitimate relationship with Sekai when Akira was still quite young.
  3. Nozomu beat his wife, possibly abused his young brother, and generally comes across as an unpleasant person. He apparently managed to keep this all hidden from his own daughter: Ami says his biggest fault was that he was too normal.
  4. Nozomu is dead and has no known living children, assuming that Akira is Ami's biological father. Sana is survived by Sara and Rin, with Akira and Ami not included because they're extended family (uncle and cousin) rather than immediate.
This is by no means compelling, but it's at least plausible, which is more than we can say for other candidates.
4. Nozomu fits the foreshadowing very well.
  • If Sensei has secret nieces, they're probably Nozomu's children, and if Nozomu has children, Sana and Rin are by far the most likely given the mystery surrounding their father.
  • Sana would already be related to the Arakawas through her dad.
  • Sensei is being compared to Sana's real dad because they would have been brothers.
  • Sensei is a father figure (but really an uncle) to Sana and Rin because he would be their only living adult male family member.
5. Nozomu fits the connection to the gods very well.
For one thing, he supposedly shares his name with one of the gods (worth noting: the only characters who have ever referred to USER1 as Nozomu are Pareidolia and a couple of shady narrators), though I don't want to identify the two Nozomus as the same entity or anything.

More importantly, connection to the gods and especially Pareidolia seems to run in the Arakawa family. Sensei has Pareidolia in his head. Sekai and Yuu both heard the voice of god(s), and Pareidolia talks like he knew them the same way he knows Sensei. After Sekai's death, her ghost is working for/with Pareidolia and her organs let Pareidolia control Kaori. Ami talks to voices and has an "infection" that almost certainly invovles Pareidolia. Even Nodoka seems to be influenced by Sekai and Pareidolia, although it isn't clear whether they actually speak to her directly.

Yumi seems to be the exception that shows you don't need to be an Arakawa (barring tinfoil theories) to have Pareidolia in your head, but the Pareidolia infection does seem to be hereditary. And given that all of Nozomu's immediate family were infected, it's pretty likely he was as well and could pass this infection on to his own children. Nozomu being Sana's father thus gives us a clean explanation for why both of them are connected to Pareidolia.

This also links Sekai with Sara and Rin's mom because all three were sexual partners of Nozomu, which could explain her infection as another instance of Sara's curse. Note also that Sara's issues have started again while she's (for a second time?) in a relationship with an Arakawa.
There are two things we know about Nozomu that Sara should have known had he been her teacher, but which don't seem to be consistent with what she has and hasn't said:
  1. Nozomu was married, but Sara thought she was in a dedicated monogamous relationship with her teacher.
  2. Nozomu's surname was Arakawa, but Sara hasn't noticed that Sensei has the same surname as her teacher.
Possible explanations and why I find them unsatisfactory:
- Sara isn't telling the full truth, either because the gods forced her to forget things or because she's lying to herself.
I don't know of any direct evidence for either of these possibilities. In any case, Haruka went to the same school and almost certainly knew who Sara's teacher was. She has no reason to lie about it, and there's no indication the gods messed with her.

- (For #1 only) Nozomu and Sekai weren't married yet or the marriage was a secret, possibly because they knew they were related.
The evidence doesn't back this up: the Xoanon says "your brother's wife" took care of wizard Akira, and Mrs. Nakayama refers to Sekai as Akira's sister-in-law in "Kyoto".

- Timeline shenanigans, for example Sara comes from a world where Nozomu and Sekai never got married.
There's no real evidence for this and it opens up a can of worms about how Sana and Ami can exist in the same timeline, especially when plenty of people remember each of them from well before the resets.

- (For #2 only) Sara doesn't know that Sensei's surname is Arakawa.
I was convinced by this one for a little while: Sara has never said the name Arakawa, and i don't think anyone has ever used it in direct conversation with her. Same is true for Haruka, who should also recognize the name of Sara's teacher. However, I found one case where Imani says it while Sara is present and implied to be paying attention.
View attachment 4997751 View attachment 4997752
In theory Sara could be too distracted to notice, but I can't see Selebus intentionally putting this in the game if he's intending a later reveal where Sara reacts to the name Arakawa.
Theory #1: Yuu was Sara's teacher and the father of Sana and Rin.
Advantages:
  • Yuu probably abandoned his family with Saki, so he wouldn't be married and might have used an assumed name so that they couldn't track him down.
  • We know for sure that Yuu had a supernatural connection and was much older than Sara, whereas we're only guessing for Nozomu.
  • Many of the clues only point toward Sana's dad being an Arakawa, which obviously fits Yuu just as much as Nozomu.
Problems:
  • Sana would have at least two living siblings (Akira and Rin), so the "survived by one other" line can't be taken literally.
  • Sara's teacher (manipulative, sexual predator, prone to anger) had a drastically different personality from young Yuu (kind, lazy).
  • Sana and Rin would be Akira's half-sisters instead of his nieces, so the foreshadowing of secret nieces would need to be explained elsewhere.
  • Pareidolia says that nobody remembers Yuu, as if all memories of his existence were erased from the terminal. While Sara might have forgotten some things, she certainly remembers far more about her teacher than Sensei does about his father.
I find this theory plausible, but I think the problems are harder to overcome than for the Nozomu theory.

Theory #2: Sara is Yuu's daughter.
There are three girls in the NiB demo: Saki, Miu, and Reina. LiL has characters that are Yuu's children with Saki (Nozomu, Akira) and with Miu (Sekai). If he also had a child with Reina, Sara is the most likely candidate as they both have dark hair and green eyes.

Advantages:
  • Explains the foreshadowing that the Arakawas and Sakakibaras are related.
  • Explains Sara's (and Sana's) supernatural connection as coming from her parents rather than her teacher.
  • Explains one secret niece (Sana), though not why Ami refers to nieces, plural.
Problems:
  • The father who raised Sara can't be Yuu - his surname and personality don't fit and he owned the bar even before Sara was born, meaning before Akira was conceived. There's no hint she's adopted - if she is I would have expected her emotionally abusive parents to rub it in her face at every opportunity.
  • The identity of Sana's father is still a mystery, especially if he also fathered Rin. Doesn't explain the foreshadowing linking him to Sensei.
  • Rin's chosen status and her mother's madness aren't explained.
I find this theory unlikely but not impossible. It's also not mutually exclusive with the theories about Sara's teacher; after all, the Arakawas are the incest family.

Theory #3: Sana secretly isn't the daughter of Sara's teacher, but rather of Sara's younger classmate Akira Arakawa.
The idea is that in her senior year Sara "cheated" on her teacher with freshman Akira, then the gods forced both of them to forget.

Advantages:
  • There are some hints that there might have been a timeline where Sara and Akira actually knew each other in high school.
    View attachment 4997760
  • Explains the foreshadowing that Sensei is like Sana's dad because he actually is her real dad (though this gets murky when they're really talking about similarities between Sensei and Sara's teacher).
Problems:
  • Leaves pretty much everything else unexplained: Sara's teacher (who would still have to be Shota's dad), Rin's parents, Sensei's nieces, etc.
  • Like with Yuu, we'd have to dismiss that Sana is "survived by one other" since Akira and Rin would both be members of her immediate family.
I don't consider this a serious possibility, I'm just including it for completeness.

Theory #4: Adult Akira was Sara's teacher thanks to alternate timelines, time travel, or some other such bullshit.
I think this one can be rejected pretty quickly: the teen Sara in "Good Boy" has a boyfriend (her teacher), but doesn't recognize Sensei at all.
TLDR: Lots of little hints can be explained if Nozomu was the father of Sana and Rin. On the other hand, parts of Sara's story about her teacher seem to be inconsistent with Nozomu. But since I find all other alternatives even less likely, I lean toward the belief that Nozomu is the father and Sara's omissions will be explained in a way that we don't yet understand.
