Pareidolia says that nobody remembers Yuu, as if all memories of his existence were erased from the terminal. While Sara might have forgotten some things, she certainly remembers far more about her teacher than Sensei does about his father.
I find this theory plausible, but I think the problems are harder to overcome than for the Nozomu theory.
Theory #2: Sara is Yuu's daughter.
Spoiler
There are three girls in the NiB demo: Saki, Miu, and Reina. LiL has characters that are Yuu's children with Saki (Nozomu, Akira) and with Miu (Sekai). If he also had a child with Reina, Sara is the most likely candidate as they both have dark hair and green eyes.
Advantages:
Explains the foreshadowing that the Arakawas and Sakakibaras are related.
Explains Sara's (and Sana's) supernatural connection as coming from her parents rather than her teacher.
Explains one secret niece (Sana), though not why Ami refers to nieces, plural.
Problems:
The father who raised Sara can't be Yuu - his surname and personality don't fit and he owned the bar even before Sara was born, meaning before Akira was conceived. There's no hint she's adopted - if she is I would have expected her emotionally abusive parents to rub it in her face at every opportunity.
The identity of Sana's father is still a mystery, especially if he also fathered Rin. Doesn't explain the foreshadowing linking him to Sensei.
Rin's chosen status and her mother's madness aren't explained.
I find this theory unlikely but not impossible. It's also not mutually exclusive with the theories about Sara's teacher; after all, the Arakawas
are
the incest family.
Theory #3: Sana secretly isn't the daughter of Sara's teacher, but rather of Sara's younger classmate Akira Arakawa.
Spoiler
The idea is that in her senior year Sara "cheated" on her teacher with freshman Akira, then the gods forced both of them to forget.
Advantages:
There are some hints that there
might
have been a timeline where Sara and Akira actually knew each other in high school.
Spoiler
View attachment 4997760
Explains the foreshadowing that Sensei is like Sana's dad because he actually is her real dad (though this gets murky when they're really talking about similarities between Sensei and Sara's teacher).
Problems:
Leaves pretty much everything else unexplained: Sara's teacher (who would still have to be Shota's dad), Rin's parents, Sensei's nieces, etc.
Like with Yuu, we'd have to dismiss that Sana is "survived by one other" since Akira and Rin would both be members of her immediate family.
I don't consider this a serious possibility, I'm just including it for completeness.
Theory #4: Adult Akira was Sara's teacher thanks to alternate timelines, time travel, or some other such bullshit.
I think this one can be rejected pretty quickly: the teen Sara in "Good Boy" has a boyfriend (her teacher), but doesn't recognize Sensei at all.
TLDR
: Lots of little hints can be explained if Nozomu was the father of Sana and Rin. On the other hand, parts of Sara's story about her teacher seem to be inconsistent with Nozomu. But since I find all other alternatives even less likely, I lean toward the belief that Nozomu is the father and Sara's omissions will be explained in a way that we don't yet understand.

spoilers.html:
1. Sara has gone through periods of the gods messing with her mind, and these seem to coincide with her two relationships.

View attachment 4997717

Although she's been keeping it a secret, recently her issues have started again. Possibly this coincides with the start of her new relationship with Sensei.

View attachment 4997699
"WHY NOW?! THIS IS SUPPOSED TO BE OVER!" (redacted dialog given in script comment)
2. The gods "know" Sara from her past and supposedly fathered Sana.
She's one of Pareidolia's favorites and he associates her with someone Sensei never met, implying he already knew Sara from before.
View attachment 4997700 View attachment 4997702
Pegasus identifies himself as Sana's father, linking him somehow to Sara's teacher.
View attachment 4997703 View attachment 4997704 View attachment 4997706
3. Sana and Rin are both "chosen" by god(s).
Like Sensei and unlike the other girls, they're allowed into Yasu's church. I think Pareidolia is the one who chose them since this happens in Chapter 3 when he's taken over Yasu's church.
View attachment 4997708 View attachment 4997709
4. I suspect the gods drove Rin's bio mom insane.
Along with Sara, Pareidolia has a second favorite who Sensei doesn't know. It makes a lot of sense for this to be Rin's bio mom: she's an important character Sensei hasn't met, she's tied to Sara through their shared baby daddy, and their children were both chosen by (probably) Pareidolia.

Rin's mom is described as psycho and virtually mute, which sounds like one of Sensei's blackouts.
View attachment 4997712 View attachment 4997713
...
View attachment 4997714
Sara experienced similar symptoms during high school, but was able to overcome them and avoid going insane. In particular she risked becoming "lost inside of herself" like a mute crazy person might.
View attachment 4997716 View attachment 4997717 View attachment 4997718
I think Rin's mom had the same curse, but wasn't so lucky; she couldn't overcome it and instead went insane.
5. The simplest way to explain all of these points is that Sara's teacher is the cause of the godfuckery.
Maybe Pegasus just happened to cuck Sara's teacher at the right moment to be the actual father of Sana. Maybe Rin's mother is just regular crazy and has no actual connection to the gods. Maybe Sara and Rin's mom just happen to share symptoms and also just happen to have been groomed by the same man. In isolation, each of these could be explained as just coincidence (though you have to question why Sel would choose to write it that way), but when considered together the series of coincidences becomes increasingly improbable.

In contrast, everything can be explained by a simple theory: Sara's teacher was "chosen" by Pareidolia, who was in his head and experienced his sexual conquests. He transmitted a supernatural curse to the people he was in relationships with. His children inherited his chosen status from him.
I'm not going to try to justify these in this post, but I have two theories regarding Pegasus that I go back and forth on:
  • Pegasus and Pareidolia are different identities assumed by the same entity (USER3).
  • Pegasus is the "ghost" of Sana's father, who struck a deal with Pareidolia.
It's even possible they both contain an element of truth. Either way I think Pegasus's claims are consistent with Sana having a human father who had Pareidolia in his head.
6. Sekai might have experienced a curse similar to Sara and Rin's mom.
Toward the end of her life, she was hearing voices and going mad. Pareidolia specifically calls it an infection.
View attachment 4997723 View attachment 4997724 View attachment 4997729 View attachment 4997731 View attachment 4997786
And Pareidolia doesn't only talk about her like he was in her head; he also lusts after her like she's another of his "favorites".
View attachment 4997732 View attachment 4997734
I don't want to draw too many conclusions from this. As Yuu's daughter, Sekai probably had a hereditary connection to the gods. Even if her curse was exacerbated by a relationship, it could have been because of Akira, who presumably had Pareidolia in his head even then. But I can't help but think that the way Pareidolia objectifies her is more likely to come from Nozomu.

spoilers.title: 3. The case for Nozomu Arakawa
spoilers.html:
1. Sana and Rin's dad is someone important to the story beyond just linking the two of them.
- He likely has an importance to the supernatural plot, based on the connection the Sakakibaras share with Rin and her mom.

- He likely has a connection to Sensei's past: He taught at Sara's high school, which from "Good Boy" is the abandoned school that keeps showing up in happy events and so must have some importance in Sensei's subconscious.

- His name is being hidden from us (and Sensei): With how much we've learned about this guy, his name should have come up at some point, similar to other off screen characters like Masahiro, Tomonori, Rie, etc. This is especially true since Sara wants to track him down and make him pay child support - she should be naming and shaming him in hopes that anyone has heard about his current whereabouts. Most likely we haven't learned the name because it would reveal something that it's too early for us to know. (Possible counterexample: I doubt the name of Haruka's husband has any importance, but he's never been referred to by name in conversations where it would be natural to do so.)

- Something needs to give his reveal impact: Finding out that Sana and Rin are sisters will be momentarily surprising, but it's not going to cause a significant change in their relationship or really affect the story. It has to come with some shocking revelation about their father in order to feel like an important twist.

- The reveal needs to happen somehow: Nobody knows who Rin's dad was except for her insane mom. Nobody knows which other girls Sara's teacher was seeing. I don't see how we get the reveal that they're the same person unless someone else (could be a god) knew the guy for a different reason. He's likely dead now (see below), in which case he can't show up to make the reveal himself.
In light of all that, I don't give serious consideration to the idea that their dad is some rando or someone who hasn't been introduced to the story at all yet.

2. Things we know about Sana's dad exclude almost all known characters.
  1. He was a high school teacher approximately fifteen years ago, which probably excludes people with known professions like Tomonori, Mr. Tojo, and Takoyaki Man.
  2. He was significantly older than Sara, which excludes a lot of random very important side characters, such as Frank: Friend of Tony: Takoyaki Son, Son of Takoyaki Man.
  3. He was a serial cheater who groomed multiple young girls while tricking Sara into thinking he was a great guy, which I think probably excludes Yuu, who consistently comes across as kind but lazy in his own thoughts (including in NiB).
  4. He's probably dead and has no living children beyond Sana and Rin, which obviously excludes all the other girls' dads. I'm basing this off the throwaway line from sports wars that Sana was "survived by" Sara and "one other", who I assume is Rin. I think this line should be taken literally - Sel had to know it would be interpreted as foreshadowing, especially when the mystery of Sana's family is clearly important, and I don't think he would put in foreshadowing that's just false.
    View attachment 4997754 View attachment 4997755
3. All of these things could be true of Nozomu.
  1. There's no direct evidence that Nozomu was a teacher, but his brother, half-sister/wife, and probably mother all were, so it's a common occupation in his family. Nozomu's wife also probably taught at the same school.
  2. We don't know Nozomu's exact age, but he was old enough to be in a legitimate relationship with Sekai when Akira was still quite young.
  3. Nozomu beat his wife, possibly abused his young brother, and generally comes across as an unpleasant person. He apparently managed to keep this all hidden from his own daughter: Ami says his biggest fault was that he was too normal.
  4. Nozomu is dead and has no known living children, assuming that Akira is Ami's biological father. Sana is survived by Sara and Rin, with Akira and Ami not included because they're extended family (uncle and cousin) rather than immediate.
This is by no means compelling, but it's at least plausible, which is more than we can say for other candidates.
4. Nozomu fits the foreshadowing very well.
  • If Sensei has secret nieces, they're probably Nozomu's children, and if Nozomu has children, Sana and Rin are by far the most likely given the mystery surrounding their father.
  • Sana would already be related to the Arakawas through her dad.
  • Sensei is being compared to Sana's real dad because they would have been brothers.
  • Sensei is a father figure (but really an uncle) to Sana and Rin because he would be their only living adult male family member.
5. Nozomu fits the connection to the gods very well.
For one thing, he supposedly shares his name with one of the gods (worth noting: the only characters who have ever referred to USER1 as Nozomu are Pareidolia and a couple of shady narrators), though I don't want to identify the two Nozomus as the same entity or anything.

More importantly, connection to the gods and especially Pareidolia seems to run in the Arakawa family. Sensei has Pareidolia in his head. Sekai and Yuu both heard the voice of god(s), and Pareidolia talks like he knew them the same way he knows Sensei. After Sekai's death, her ghost is working for/with Pareidolia and her organs let Pareidolia control Kaori. Ami talks to voices and has an "infection" that almost certainly invovles Pareidolia. Even Nodoka seems to be influenced by Sekai and Pareidolia, although it isn't clear whether they actually speak to her directly.

Yumi seems to be the exception that shows you don't need to be an Arakawa (barring tinfoil theories) to have Pareidolia in your head, but the Pareidolia infection does seem to be hereditary. And given that all of Nozomu's immediate family were infected, it's pretty likely he was as well and could pass this infection on to his own children. Nozomu being Sana's father thus gives us a clean explanation for why both of them are connected to Pareidolia.

This also links Sekai with Sara and Rin's mom because all three were sexual partners of Nozomu, which could explain her infection as another instance of Sara's curse. Note also that Sara's issues have started again while she's (for a second time?) in a relationship with an Arakawa.

I don't see how we get the reveal that they're the same person unless someone else (could be a god) knew the guy for a different reason. He's likely dead now (see below), in which case he can't show up to make the reveal himself.

spoilers.title: 4. Problems with the Nozomu theory
spoilers.html:
There are two things we know about Nozomu that Sara should have known had he been her teacher, but which don't seem to be consistent with what she has and hasn't said:
  1. Nozomu was married, but Sara thought she was in a dedicated monogamous relationship with her teacher.
  2. Nozomu's surname was Arakawa, but Sara hasn't noticed that Sensei has the same surname as her teacher.
Possible explanations and why I find them unsatisfactory:
- Sara isn't telling the full truth, either because the gods forced her to forget things or because she's lying to herself.
I don't know of any direct evidence for either of these possibilities. In any case, Haruka went to the same school and almost certainly knew who Sara's teacher was. She has no reason to lie about it, and there's no indication the gods messed with her.

- (For #1 only) Nozomu and Sekai weren't married yet or the marriage was a secret, possibly because they knew they were related.
The evidence doesn't back this up: the Xoanon says "your brother's wife" took care of wizard Akira, and Mrs. Nakayama refers to Sekai as Akira's sister-in-law in "Kyoto".

- Timeline shenanigans, for example Sara comes from a world where Nozomu and Sekai never got married.
There's no real evidence for this and it opens up a can of worms about how Sana and Ami can exist in the same timeline, especially when plenty of people remember each of them from well before the resets.

- (For #2 only) Sara doesn't know that Sensei's surname is Arakawa.
I was convinced by this one for a little while: Sara has never said the name Arakawa, and i don't think anyone has ever used it in direct conversation with her. Same is true for Haruka, who should also recognize the name of Sara's teacher. However, I found one case where Imani says it while Sara is present and implied to be paying attention.
View attachment 4997751 View attachment 4997752
In theory Sara could be too distracted to notice, but I can't see Selebus intentionally putting this in the game if he's intending a later reveal where Sara reacts to the name Arakawa.

spoilers.title: 5. Alternate Theories
spoilers.html:
Theory #1: Yuu was Sara's teacher and the father of Sana and Rin.
Advantages:
  • Yuu probably abandoned his family with Saki, so he wouldn't be married and might have used an assumed name so that they couldn't track him down.
  • We know for sure that Yuu had a supernatural connection and was much older than Sara, whereas we're only guessing for Nozomu.
  • Many of the clues only point toward Sana's dad being an Arakawa, which obviously fits Yuu just as much as Nozomu.
Problems:
  • Sana would have at least two living siblings (Akira and Rin), so the "survived by one other" line can't be taken literally.
  • Sara's teacher (manipulative, sexual predator, prone to anger) had a drastically different personality from young Yuu (kind, lazy).
  • Sana and Rin would be Akira's half-sisters instead of his nieces, so the foreshadowing of secret nieces would need to be explained elsewhere.
  • Pareidolia says that nobody remembers Yuu, as if all memories of his existence were erased from the terminal. While Sara might have forgotten some things, she certainly remembers far more about her teacher than Sensei does about his father.
I find this theory plausible, but I think the problems are harder to overcome than for the Nozomu theory.

Theory #2: Sara is Yuu's daughter.
There are three girls in the NiB demo: Saki, Miu, and Reina. LiL has characters that are Yuu's children with Saki (Nozomu, Akira) and with Miu (Sekai). If he also had a child with Reina, Sara is the most likely candidate as they both have dark hair and green eyes.

Advantages:
  • Explains the foreshadowing that the Arakawas and Sakakibaras are related.
  • Explains Sara's (and Sana's) supernatural connection as coming from her parents rather than her teacher.
  • Explains one secret niece (Sana), though not why Ami refers to nieces, plural.
Problems:
  • The father who raised Sara can't be Yuu - his surname and personality don't fit and he owned the bar even before Sara was born, meaning before Akira was conceived. There's no hint she's adopted - if she is I would have expected her emotionally abusive parents to rub it in her face at every opportunity.
  • The identity of Sana's father is still a mystery, especially if he also fathered Rin. Doesn't explain the foreshadowing linking him to Sensei.
  • Rin's chosen status and her mother's madness aren't explained.
I find this theory unlikely but not impossible. It's also not mutually exclusive with the theories about Sara's teacher; after all, the Arakawas are the incest family.

Theory #3: Sana secretly isn't the daughter of Sara's teacher, but rather of Sara's younger classmate Akira Arakawa.
The idea is that in her senior year Sara "cheated" on her teacher with freshman Akira, then the gods forced both of them to forget.

Advantages:
  • There are some hints that there might have been a timeline where Sara and Akira actually knew each other in high school.
    View attachment 4997760
  • Explains the foreshadowing that Sensei is like Sana's dad because he actually is her real dad (though this gets murky when they're really talking about similarities between Sensei and Sara's teacher).
Problems:
  • Leaves pretty much everything else unexplained: Sara's teacher (who would still have to be Shota's dad), Rin's parents, Sensei's nieces, etc.
  • Like with Yuu, we'd have to dismiss that Sana is "survived by one other" since Akira and Rin would both be members of her immediate family.
I don't consider this a serious possibility, I'm just including it for completeness.

Theory #4: Adult Akira was Sara's teacher thanks to alternate timelines, time travel, or some other such bullshit.
I think this one can be rejected pretty quickly: the teen Sara in "Good Boy" has a boyfriend (her teacher), but doesn't recognize Sensei at all.

Many of the clues only point toward Sana's dad being an Arakawa, which obviously fits Yuu just as much as Nozomu.
Problems:
Sana would have at least two living siblings (Akira and Rin), so the "survived by one other" line can't be taken literally.
Sara's teacher (manipulative, sexual predator, prone to anger) had a drastically different personality from young Yuu (kind, lazy).
Sana and Rin would be Akira's half-sisters instead of his nieces, so the foreshadowing of secret nieces would need to be explained elsewhere.
Pareidolia says that nobody remembers Yuu, as if all memories of his existence were erased from the terminal. While Sara might have forgotten some things, she certainly remembers far more about her teacher than Sensei does about his father.

spoilers.html:
There are three girls in the NiB demo: Saki, Miu, and Reina. LiL has characters that are Yuu's children with Saki (Nozomu, Akira) and with Miu (Sekai). If he also had a child with Reina, Sara is the most likely candidate as they both have dark hair and green eyes.

Advantages:
  • Explains the foreshadowing that the Arakawas and Sakakibaras are related.
  • Explains Sara's (and Sana's) supernatural connection as coming from her parents rather than her teacher.
  • Explains one secret niece (Sana), though not why Ami refers to nieces, plural.
Problems:
  • The father who raised Sara can't be Yuu - his surname and personality don't fit and he owned the bar even before Sara was born, meaning before Akira was conceived. There's no hint she's adopted - if she is I would have expected her emotionally abusive parents to rub it in her face at every opportunity.
  • The identity of Sana's father is still a mystery, especially if he also fathered Rin. Doesn't explain the foreshadowing linking him to Sensei.
  • Rin's chosen status and her mother's madness aren't explained.

  • Chika & Chinami's new apartment
  • Akira's new apartment

*All 4 missable scenes require that you got the Sara scene from the last "Nodokathon". If you haven't, you'll get three crossed-out events.

07 - Maya 1 (Monday night - dorms)
08 - Maya 2 (Linked)

16 - Niki 3 (Linked)

Bonus animations are:

posts.content_html_raw:
Initial thoughts about the update:
- Sara and Ayane's interaction was sweet. It's good to see Ayane venting for once. Sara took the whole situation more or less how I'd expect her to, and it makes sense involving her past. One thing I'm kind of lamenting is that we still don't get to know if it was Nozomu. What we learned about him both support (he blamed Akira for the mind issues of Yuu - assumed - and also freaked out on Sara when he found out about her stuff) and go against the theory (he's far too passive in sex).

In regard to Sara's reconnection with Sana, I think it makes sense to approach it from the angle Sana did. But I, personally, am never buying it. She did it to be cruel and she's a piece of shit. Ayane said it best. If she was trying to "include" Sara or whatever she'd have talked to her first.
------------------------------------------------------------------

- Yumi's with Pareidolia confirmed. And can resist gods like a champ. I wonder if her being tainted is because she's with Pareidolia or whatever happened with HOPE and the end of the last reset.
------------------------------------------------------------------

- Maya's deal with the boxes just never ends, does it? A bit of a misdirection there with Ami sending her to deliver boxes but that was just manipulation to get Akira, I think. That Maya couldn't open the box maybe means that she's blocking something related to Maya Prime, same as Akira?
------------------------------------------------------------------

- Yuki was... well, I can't say it's just for shock value, because it does fit with everything that was told before about the characters involved. But I love Yuki's character and am very pissed that I had to go through that. Particularly, I question the decision of "I don't want to cut ties with Yumi, but will have everyone here gangbang her mother and then throw her naked outside" ????? I'm sorry, what? That part makes zero sense to me.

The one thing about the entire scene that I'm choosing to focus on is Tsubasa. Here's why: Tsubasa is likely the girl that ran with the gang for a while and taught Yuki English, thus her calling Tsubasa "nee-chan" (it's very unlikely they're actual sisters). But why is Tsubasa there? Well, remember how Kaori/Sekaori learned of Yuki's plight? Tsubasa is now in a partnership with Himawari, thus I think the link is there. Furthermore, although extremely tragic, brutal and distasteful (to say the least), what happened to Yuki fits what Himawari says 100%.

Think about it, isn't this the whole suffering thing Himawari says they have to go through so that things can work out in the end? There is the brutal gangrape scene and then who's waiting for Yuki outside exactly as she comes out of it, as if on cue? Tsubasa (also called the collector, sort of). I think the scene is very telling. I'm not suggesting that Himawari or the gods set things up so Yuki could get gangraped, but instead that they set things up so she could have support immediately after it happened. Because, again, as tragic as it is, it is their understanding that they have to go through these tragedies, they'll just try to soften them as they can.
------------------------------------------------------------------

- Noriko, Ami and Niki situation

Well, this was just expected wasn't it? Does it hurt that Niki and Akira """broke up"""? Yes. Yes, it does. But I had pointed this out, Selebus wrote himself into a narrative corner by having Niki move in with him - because her character cannot accept all this shit and yet he placed her there. So now we have this new situation where it's feasible that she'd be there and know about things.

Ami is just... yeah, can't even comment on that tbh. She's doing it with everyone. I'm just happy Akira is FINALLY seeing it. Also kudos for Akira for finally standing up for himself in the worst way possible lol I mean that he didn't stop fucking Noriko regardless of what happened.

And Noriko finally got laid, god bless her. The funny part was that she behaved like a gacha character or something. She got semen in her and gained a new skin basically she's wearing a totally different outfit the morning after for the first time.
------------------------------------------------------------------

Lastly, the Nozomu stuff. I'm glad he didn't rape Akira, and the way Sekai entered Akira's life clearly explains a lot. It also explains why he's so spineless - it was beaten out of him from a young age. I'm curious about what happened to Saki and Yuu, and why Nozomu blamed Akira for it.

One very important point though is WHY THE FUCK would Sekai STAY with Nozomu after this. Given that she was either just his girlfriend or fiancee at this point. One might say "well, she stayed so she could protect Akira", but there surely were a million better ways to do that without being involved with Nozomu. Another point is that the whole "Nozomu being a god" and Akira seeing him as a god due to the abuse is worth noting.

I like the "I won, he's dead and I'm not" though. If only Akira got a spine back.
This is a list of things that got clarified/revealed.

1. Sekai rescued Akira from hell before she groomed him. Which explains why he can't ever make up his mind with her being just a predator, or being able to not feel gratitude towards her.

2. People all know about Sekai having sex with him. Niki's parents knew, Niki knew, Noriko knows, Maya knows.

3. Ami has always known about the resets, but has chosen to preserve the peace behind Akira's back. This is why she feels superior to everyone else and asks things like if they'd die for him. Furthermore, she lost Sekai to the gods (she lost her mind a year before her death), and is always trying to not lose Akira to the gods too. I think it's likely that she has no powers, as she stated - and being able to navigate the resets as she does comes from skill instead, which makes her pride make more sense. That she mentions herself dying to Akira, also aligns with the idea of the resets ending due to her death.

4. Kaori/Sekaori, Himawari and Tsubasa might be all connected.

5. Nozomu was better than Akira at everything and abused him to a brutal extent out of anger for something he caused to Yuu and Saki? Sekai somehow kept Nozomu in check. It's unclear if Ami knows this about Nozomu.

6. Sara DID NOT take any deals from either Pegasus or the god that helps Akira out of the AUTOPILOT. This conflicts with Pegasus telling Sana that he fucked Sara. If Sara is telling the truth, that makes the gods calling her a whore strange. Maybe it's because she gave herself to Nozomu (another god?). The gods mention ascension to Yumi after all, maybe one can just ascend.

7. The TSS alludes to being in a space WAY in the future compared to the resets. If that's particular to Yumi's or to the TSS as a whole remains to be seen. Sekaori also mentions the ability to stop Yuki's time.
Those are my initial thoughts. Usually I let it sit a while and make a more structured post, but I had to digest a few things through writing this time. All in all, solid update, tbh this is what an update should be like.
I think the one thing that is out of the norm is Yuki's gangbang, and that is pretty much what we can expect from a dark route. Meaning to take the worst possible outcome of a given situation and show it all.

As I read it, I kept thinking to myself: Is this really necessary in terms of narrative? And I still don't know. I don't think it's unreasonable to think that a degree of that would happen, but would the gangbang itself? Or was that just for shock value?

This is not the sort of question I'd like to be asking when I read a story, as it did not happen during "stomachache" or the more recent Sana stuff. Those were hard to read events, but I didn't start questioning the narrative validity of those events during them. I'll try to focus on other stuff, I guess - or take other people's perspectives.

I do wish I hadn't had to have seen that done to a character I love though. Hopefully what comes out of it justifies the difference between stopping at giving a blowjob and prostating herself, to full-on gangbang and thrown into the street naked, bruised and covered in semen.
Edit: My question about the requirements was cleared up by TheGoodPastor.

posts.content_html_raw:
Moonflare said:
I often forget that Yuki still has to redeem herself. Thing is, she has to redeem herself to Yumi (in my eyes). Not to me. I never needed for her to be gangraped in order to get money for her cancer treatment, to be there for Yumi for a few more years, in order for me to go, okay, now I get that you care.

How does this prove to Yumi that she cares in the first place? Yumi wasn't there. Will she go "wow, my mom got gangraped for me, what a mom" (and that's before taking into account that Yumi is aware that things are on a fucking loop and time resets, which potentially makes it pointless) - and since I'm already bashing on it, let's talk about how cancer treatment wouldn't even be that expensive?

I feel like this has got to be yet another aspect of health care that is heavily based on the US rather than Japan. Japan has "free" universal healthcare (you pay 30% of total costs). What Yuki would have to pay for treatment is covered by a normal job, given that she doesn't have to provide for anyone else. It would not be a crippling debt.

Even if she can't work, Akira could pay for her, or Sara, or anyone else. You don't need a Yazuka boss to do it. I do get why she'd go with the route that she has always gone with, but yeah, I'm too salty about one my favorite characters having that done to her to think clearly.
In the words of Conan: "Crom Selebus, I have never prayed to you before. I have no tongue for it. But if you grant me one thing, grant me this: grant me revenge."
Click to expand...
Yeah sadly I think her core flaw she needs to get over is her pride. She won't admit it to herself, and she will keep saying that she thinks she is a piece of shit, but she does have a twisted sense of pride from being the Dragon.

Even in this update it potentially bites her in the ass as she tells off Boss Yamaguchi even though she came there knowing he has all the leverage. You can't really blame her, but she's latched onto it for too long and let it become her chain. She started on the journey but even then she half-assed it. She's too cool for friends, too badass for a bar job, too broken for love, too fucked up to be a parent. She continues to state that it's what she deserves, but is that really all the truth?

The drug addiction is a vice for sure, but it's a scapegoat for true issue. The way I see it, the end of her journey is for her to break her "chains" and put aside her facade of self-pity and pride and learn to embrace that it's okay to be a friend, a co-worker, a sappy lover, and most importantly a mother.

In her mind being "real" lowers the only thing that has given her life value, the persona of the Dragon. She can state all she wants how she should've been a better mom and blame it on the drugs, but she's already shown that she has the fortitude quit them no problem only to relapse when things didn't go her way.

Only when she finally realizes that the Dragon isn't the real her (or at least not ALL that she is) she can hang up the suit for good and actually face her problems. She can pour her heart out to her daughter, give heartfelt gratitute to her friends, accept the younger acquaintence's advances and possibly even find love. She can ask help from someone else instead of foolishly going to the yakuza and her abuser where she knows the terms won't be in her favor. Perhaps this latest humilation and trauma will be her turning point? Idk...

Yuki could either be the catalyst that causes Yumi to realize her own worth, or vice versa. Since if you think about it, Yumi's problem is practically a shadow of her mom's. Yumi's persona lies in the Delinquent, it's the only thing that has given her attention when she had nothing, it made people see her. Even if they hate or fear her, at least she exists in someone's eyes. She can't have friends because she's gotta be badass, she can't TRY to find a job because it's not cool, she can't be in love because that will crack her persona.

Once again, I have no idea where Selebus plans to go with Yuki from here but I'm sure he will continue to surprise me (for better or worse.) These are just musings of what would satisfy me narratively.

spoilers.title: Ramblings on Yuki as a whole
spoilers.html:
Yeah sadly I think her core flaw she needs to get over is her pride. She won't admit it to herself, and she will keep saying that she thinks she is a piece of shit, but she does have a twisted sense of pride from being the Dragon.

Even in this update it potentially bites her in the ass as she tells off Boss Yamaguchi even though she came there knowing he has all the leverage. You can't really blame her, but she's latched onto it for too long and let it become her chain. She started on the journey but even then she half-assed it. She's too cool for friends, too badass for a bar job, too broken for love, too fucked up to be a parent. She continues to state that it's what she deserves, but is that really all the truth?

The drug addiction is a vice for sure, but it's a scapegoat for true issue. The way I see it, the end of her journey is for her to break her "chains" and put aside her facade of self-pity and pride and learn to embrace that it's okay to be a friend, a co-worker, a sappy lover, and most importantly a mother.

In her mind being "real" lowers the only thing that has given her life value, the persona of the Dragon. She can state all she wants how she should've been a better mom and blame it on the drugs, but she's already shown that she has the fortitude quit them no problem only to relapse when things didn't go her way.

Only when she finally realizes that the Dragon isn't the real her (or at least not ALL that she is) she can hang up the suit for good and actually face her problems. She can pour her heart out to her daughter, give heartfelt gratitute to her friends, accept the younger acquaintence's advances and possibly even find love. She can ask help from someone else instead of foolishly going to the yakuza and her abuser where she knows the terms won't be in her favor. Perhaps this latest humilation and trauma will be her turning point? Idk...

Yuki could either be the catalyst that causes Yumi to realize her own worth, or vice versa. Since if you think about it, Yumi's problem is practically a shadow of her mom's. Yumi's persona lies in the Delinquent, it's the only thing that has given her attention when she had nothing, it made people see her. Once again, I have no idea where Selebus plans to go with Yuki from here but I'm sure he will continue to surprise me (for better or worse.) These are just musings of what would satisfy me narratively.

I love Yuki. My reaction is just that I don't want to see people I love being brutally hurt. The girls and Akira hurt eachother under a cloak of consent. Their perception to what's being done is skewed, and thus more acceptable to the viewer - because they do it while thinking they're loving eachother while doing it.

This is one of the main points that Niki raises in this update: "Sure, now, it might seem like the potential damage is contained. But look at yourself, Akira, and tell me if decades later that remains true." The damage that they're doing to eachother takes a very long time to take effect to the extent that it would become clear. The immediate reaction of a young girl in a relationship with him doesn't seem that destructive by itself, it's just a very bad choice. But then, check back years later and that same girl had the opportunity to develop a healthy mindset taken from her, like Sara.

And after that conversation, I tend to think that Akira's right and maybe the rational thing here is chemical castration. Won't happen because this is an adult game and he's the protagonist, but logically it is a good choice. Not only for others, but to himself as well - as it would force him to develop other coping mechanisms (which could be a good thing with enough guidance).

I reacted very emotionally because there isn't any consent in Yuki's case. There's no "even though this isn't a good relationship choice, I still want it". There's just a shell of a woman, subjecting herself to abuse because she needs money for cancer treatment. Nothing about this softens the blow. In fact, Selebus thinks that isn't enough, and doubles down by having her gang-raped.

In the first half of the scene, Yuki's still in control, even though she hates what she's having to do. I think less people would have problems with that. Disgusting? yes. But within the bounds of what one can stomach to sit through. But the second part is just torture. She has no control, she's just a victim, and we have to watch her being broken beyond compare.

It's the sort of thing that is haunting and that I wish I didn't have to see. But we're all adults here, it's fiction, and we'll move past it.

spoilers.title: Yuki vs Akira
spoilers.html:
I love Yuki. My reaction is just that I don't want to see people I love being brutally hurt. The girls and Akira hurt eachother under a cloak of consent. Their perception to what's being done is skewed, and thus more acceptable to the viewer - because they do it while thinking they're loving eachother while doing it.

This is one of the main points that Niki raises in this update: "Sure, now, it might seem like the potential damage is contained. But look at yourself, Akira, and tell me if decades later that remains true." The damage that they're doing to eachother takes a very long time to take effect to the extent that it would become clear. The immediate reaction of a young girl in a relationship with him doesn't seem that destructive by itself, it's just a very bad choice. But then, check back years later and that same girl had the opportunity to develop a healthy mindset taken from her, like Sara.

And after that conversation, I tend to think that Akira's right and maybe the rational thing here is chemical castration. Won't happen because this is an adult game and he's the protagonist, but logically it is a good choice. Not only for others, but to himself as well - as it would force him to develop other coping mechanisms (which could be a good thing with enough guidance).

I reacted very emotionally because there isn't any consent in Yuki's case. There's no "even though this isn't a good relationship choice, I still want it". There's just a shell of a woman, subjecting herself to abuse because she needs money for cancer treatment. Nothing about this softens the blow. In fact, Selebus thinks that isn't enough, and doubles down by having her gang-raped.

I do hate what happened to Yuki, and I do want that place to be burned and for every single individual who participated in making Yuki suffer to be burned at the stake. But if then Akira gets to simply romance Yuki after this, how could it be satisfying in any way?

If Tsubasa does help Yuki, then I would hate to then see Akira insert himself in the situation after everything was solved, and then for some reason Yuki falling in love with his dick simply because it is so much more better than her limp-dicked husband.

I know I'm getting mad about something that isn't even confirmed is going to happen, and fighting invisible daemons, but it is because from a meta perspective I know that we are approaching the harem ending and Selebus has to make it make sense in some way, which is why I can't help but think that everyone is going to be collected served in a silver plater for Akira to feast upon without having to change or do anything meaningful for them.

I'm honestly feeling kinda meh about this. I was invested at the beginning but then lost interest. I guess it works as a parallel to what happened at the hotel, the Sakakibaras are "bonding" while the Arakawas and adjacents are fracturing. Who knows, maybe they win the competition and get Akira to move on with them. That would certainly deal a heavy blow to Ami.

What happened to Sara was horrible, but it gets overshadowed by what happened to Yuki, and the relevations of Akira's abuse. Honestly does Selebus has a gangrape fetish? Tsubasa had one but I don't know if it was just gangbang, it happened to Imani, supposedly happened to Chika in that other dimension, and now Yuki. You can tell he was itching to also include another gangrape scene with Sara's past, but I guess even he thought that was a bit too far and opted for just physical abuse.

I know this was meant to portrait Sekai as a guardian angel of some sorts, and at least it helped explain why Akira fell so hard for her, but still that doesn't mean she isn't a monster herself. As someone who has never experienced neither, I don't want to say being sexually abused is better than physically abused, but clearly Akira prefers one over the other. One grounds him in reality, there is no way to escape because pain is what keeps you alive, but at least the other allows him to feel pleasure and numb everything else.

He got two experience both of the worst at a very young age, it maybe goes even further depending on how his mother treated him. One was simply the lesser evil.

What confuses me is their relationship. It seemed more to me like she wore the pants in the relationship. But it was implied before that Nozomu also physically abused Sekai. It was also mentioned in a weird way, as if implying "are you jealous?" despite knowing about Nozomu's abuse of Akira


During the beginning of that happy event it was also implied that Akira was being both physically and sexually abused, but before this update I thought the physical part was from part of his mother, and sexual part from Sekai.

Now that we know he was being beaten and pissed on by his brother, it just makes Sekai's flashback commentary here so much weirder.

Is like imagine if there are two raped victims and of them says to the other "He raped me today instead of you, are you jealous?" Not a 1-1 comparison, but that's the way I can explain why it irks me.

Considering Nozomu blamed Akira for whatever happened to Yuu and Saki, I think I can theorize
This is the way I imagine things went:

Nozomu and Akira are half brothers. Nozomu is Yuu's and Saki's son. Akira is the son born from an affair Yuu had. Then why don't Saki and Nozomu hate Yuu? and instead they hate Akira? perhaps because he is the only outlet for the hatred they have.

Something happened to Yuu, and it probably has something to do with Akira's mother. If I can speculate even further, Akira's mother might have killed Yuu and then herself. Saki hated Akira because he is the reason why she lost her husband, and the physical manifestation of his infedelity. Nozomu hated Akira because his very existence is the reason why his family was destroyed.

It might be too much speculation but I think it would parallel nicely with Ami's situation. Akira hated the idea of Sekai having a child, because it would rob him of something he always yearned: mother's love.

After Ami was born, everything was "fine" for 7 years, but in some way or another, Nozomu found out (or at least suspected) that Ami wasn't his daughter. Who else would he blame but Akira for destroying yet another family? Perhaps Nozomu was planning on killing him, but it ended up with both him and Sekai dying in an accident. Now Akira had to take care of whom he believed to be the daughter of the person he hated and the person he loved. What a comedy, what a tragedy.

Perhaps him shutting down after Sekai's death wasn't just because he crippled with depression. Maybe that was also his way of protecting Ami, so he didn't take his anger on her as his "mother" and "brother" did on him.

I'll think and write about the Nakayamas situation another time.

I'm curious about Zuko's opinion, he was one of the people who most wanted to see Akira have sex with Noriko, I'm curious about his opinion on whether it was a fair exchange or not.
Click to expand...
Fuckkkkk man, I’m so conflicted… Because like… wow. The way Akira opened up to Noriko about his brother was really well done, and the sex that followed was honestly kinda hot. Better yet, it didn’t abruptly end this time! Noriko got her W.

But… the trade-off… Yeahh… It left a bitter aftertaste…

I love both Nakayamas equally, so while I’m glad Noriko finally succeeded, I was sad to see it cause so much pain to the other. Niki has done so much for Akira and tried to do the same for Ami, only for her hopes and dreams to be continuously spat upon. It sucks, dude. I don’t like seeing it at all. But it needed to happen at some point.

Do I think the trade-off was fair? Narratively? Yes. If Noriko got cucked again instead, I honestly would have been genuinely annoyed. Still, it doesn’t mean I like watching Niki suffer…

Fucking Ami… Akira too. I’m glad he didn’t let Noriko’s night get ruined yet again, but like… surely there’s a more tactful solution out there than continuing to pound away.

As far as the rest of the update goes:

My overall feelings first of all: I don’t feel pleasant.

Oh don’t get me wrong, I thought the update was very solid. I loved the majority of it, even. But as far as my subjective feelings go? I feel kinda icky and disappointed. Usually after an update, I feel at least one positive thing that I can cling onto afterwards.

This update didn’t really have that.

Let’s review, shall we?

Sara - Feels worthless as a mother. Has a daughter with little respect for her, despite what Sana’s justifications may try and tell you. If you respect your mother, you don’t take advantage of their kindness or put them on blast in front of your peers knowingly.

Noriko - Finally gets a W, but with an ultra harsh caveat… Her relationship with Niki is gonna be mega awkward going forward.

posts.content_html_raw:
So something that stuck out at me about this update:

"laundry and stuff" Akira knew she had cancer, but Yuki said the money was for "laundry and stuff," not medical expenses. When Kaori found out, Yuki again asked for money for "laundry and stuff". She wanted drugs. And based on the amount she was trying to get from her husband, she wanted a life-ending amount of drugs. That was her solution. Finality.

At the end of the final event, she addresses Tsubasa as Nee-sama. Big Sister. If Yuki needed money for medical expenses, she could have gone to Tsubasa, and she would have gotten it. She wanted oblivion. That's the only thing that could have made her swallow her pride to beg her husband for money.

The implications of "Nee-sama" are huge. That means she grew up in Tsukasa's shoes, and that doesn't bode well for Tsukasa at all.

I think that other than Yuki's last event, this is what every update should be: a group of events that advance the story.
Not every update can be happy funtimes, this was definitely a darker one. And that's fine. Other updates should be more on the comical or happy side. And they'll balance each other out.

What we definitely do not need are either updates so bland we have nothing to talk about afterwards, or stuff like last update which at times feels like Selebus forgot how to write. In that sense, this one was definitely better.

Was it a polished darker update? That's up for debate, still mostly regarding Yuki's situation. I don't know that I agree 100% with Selebus' implied "obsession" with gangrape, and (violent) rape in general lately - but it's undeniable that this was an aspect that didn't exist in the story for most of its run and now it's becoming commonplace.

Thus, I do second what many people said, especially Zuko, in the sense that thinking back, the effect Selebus created with this update was that of a burden. Not a "wow, that was heavy scene portrayed masterfully", but a "was this really necessary?" - and that is something that has been surfacing a lot in chapter 4.
That being said, I think Selebus may have lost his hand for the balance of this one. He had one event overshadowing everything else (which is only a problem if you're playing update by update of course, and I do wonder how chapter 4 will feel like when we're able to play it entirely in one go).

*Also, I ran out of reactions a while back. A shame since there have been a lot of good posts since then.

Undoubtedly it's the most uncomfortable an update/chunk of events has made me. Bouncing off from Sana in dorm wars I figured I was in for a grim time there but almost every other facet of the update is what feels like it will stick with me for a while.

The way Sensei spoke to Niki at the end of her chain (as well as his decision to keep fucking, particularly given it's the most we've seen of his spine) was very disappointing to me, and his lack of growth (and backpedalling) is starting to really grate me. I know some people here are probably just happy to see Noriko get laid - or else take some solace in that silver lining - but for a variety of reasons I couldn't give less of a shit about that. I really hope there's some consequences to Noriko and Niki's relationship from this and that things aren't just treated as "awkward".

The story being negative isn't inherently negative as far as the quality of the story, though, and overall I'd say I liked the update. Most of it was very well written - which is the aspect of the game I fell in love with in the first place - and I'm happy to see the story's actually progressing again. Loved the TSS, too.

I will echo Moonflare's sentiment though, in that I'm not convinced Yuki's gangrape was wholly in service to the story. Feels like there's plenty of ways to achieve the result without going to that extreme.

May I ask why would a japanese person dislike this update?
Click to expand...
The Yuki events, actually. It's different fandoms and years ago, so it's probably a dated example, but it is what it is.
In the Danmachi light novels, after the whole Ishtar situation happened, a fox girl that used to be Ishtar's became a party member and, as is the case with light novels, harem candidate for the protagonist. However, because Ishtar's shtick was managing the red-light district, and the fox girl was one of the workers there, the fans started complaining about "used goods". It got so bad that the author had to shoehorn an explicit explanation about why she was still a virgin.

Now, I know it's different in LiL because Yuki is both a mother and used to run with the yakuza, but the japanese audience have certain, let's say, expectations of genres. And even with Yuki's past, there's a certain out-of-sight, out-of-mind mentality that would've been shattered with this update.

posts.content_html_raw:
It might be true that dark thing after dark thing happened during this update, but honestly I didn't feel it quite as much.

I think that's bad from a reader's perspective, I kinda dissasociated from everything that was happening. Not completely, but like my level of emotions wasn't equivalent to what was happening on screen. I still felt anger and sadness, but not as intense as it should've been.

It didn't reach the shock and despair I had during Molly's Lavender's Green, clicking the unclikable option dozens of times hoping something else would happen.
The dread of Karin possibly being raped.
or the sadness & disgust I felt during Stomachache.
During all of those, every click to progress the story felt heavy and painful.

Something I remember from a long time ago was the first time I read Tsuneyo's stand-up comedy event. It made me feel so uncomfortable that Tsuneyo would bring up that incident in front of everyone, that I literally had to stop and walk away for a few minutes before I could keep going. That event is nothing comparable to what happened in 0.50. And yet I had such a much stronger emotional reaction to it.

It might just be a me thing, but that's how I'm feeling at the moment.
Like, it is kinda scary how little I cared for these characters I have grown to love for years.
I think I either need to stop playing for like half a year and come back, or replay the game again so that I remember why I fell in love with these characters.

But for now, I'll reserve my judgement until beach.

I still think it was a great update. Is just that sadly my emotional investment is not matching the relevations, and suffering they endured.

spoilers.title: A personal take
spoilers.html:
I think the one thing that is out of the norm is Yuki's gangbang, and that is pretty much what we can expect from a dark route. Meaning to take the worst possible outcome of a given situation and show it all.

As I read it, I kept thinking to myself: Is this really necessary in terms of narrative? And I still don't know. I don't think it's unreasonable to think that a degree of that would happen, but would the gangbang itself? Or was that just for shock value?

This is not the sort of question I'd like to be asking when I read a story, as it did not happen during "stomachache" or the more recent Sana stuff. Those were hard to read events, but I didn't start questioning the narrative validity of those events during them. I'll try to focus on other stuff, I guess - or take other people's perspectives.

I do wish I hadn't had to have seen that done to a character I love though. Hopefully what comes out of it justifies the difference between stopping at giving a blowjob and prostating herself, to full-on gangbang and thrown into the street naked, bruised and covered in semen.

I dunno lads, either I'm just tired tired, or Sel is losing his mojo. Chapter 4 has been the worst in terms of moving the plot forward. I know Sel doesn't like upsetting the status-quo, but fuck me, something has to move in relation to the main fucking character! Or the story! Or anything at this point!

Chika losing her shit and breaking - good, yes, awesome - she is so fucking irrelevant now that it hurts.

Maya agreeing to learn shit about "old Maya" and actually being a supportive girlfriend - amazing, cool, yeah - that was stated how long ago? 3 updates? 4? Still hasn't done shit. Except agreeing to Ami threesome only to be molested by her during the reset and getting openly cucked.

Niki moving in and wanting to change something - holy fuck yes, that is very promising! - it didn't change shit. Invites are still a thing and Akira deflowered a girl on the couch while she's at home. And from what I've read - it's even less relevant now, coz Ami's a fucking cunt.

Ami being an insufferable incest goblin - hasn't she always been? Since like chapter 2? Della was one of the best events of Ch4 and I was hoping that Ami would see some change moving forward, but not "more of the same psycho manipulative bitch" change. That's not a fucking change, she literally was doing the same abusive shit in Chapter 3.

Sana turning into a nympho - yeaah, okay, a bit of a stretch, but sure - aaaand she's just unhinged now. I get being horny, I get being destructively horny, but that stunt at Sensei's house and with Sara in 0.49 is just... Not very believable. Molly is destructively horny, so she does stupid shit like trying to actively seduce her teacher, lashing out at a girl who's fucking her crush and rationalizing her own rape. Pros:
Tsubasa is interesting and mysterious.

Kyoto is insanely good.
Sekai is really interesting.

The rest of the cast are doing jack shit for almost 2 years real time. Chapter 3 ended in October 2023.

I'll try to be synthetic. I've finished the update yesterday, I passed out right after with a migraine (codeine wasn't strong enough...), so I write this now, 24 hour after my play.
Also, don't open these spoiler if you hadn't done the last update (0.50).

To be absolutely honest, her last event was nearly «perfect». Not in the «lust» sense, but the narrative one. This update contain a lot of flashback (Sara and Sensei), with some really traumatic experiences in their past. Most writing for Sensei, some scene for Sara, you get the picture. Yuki's past had to be showed in other way. And, hear me out, that way was the best and the worst. Not because of the shocking value, but because, without showing it, we know her past. We understand their dynamics.

But we have a NAME. The perpetrator have a name. And, that fact change everything. He exist. He's tangible in a narrative way. So, now, he is important in the story.

And for those who seek revenge by Yuki, I don't think you'll get one. That's not her purpose.

Yumi gonna do it. I'm sure of it.

I don't know how, but she gonna confront her father. Will she kill him? Insult him? Attack him? I don't know, but she will do something.

What can I say? She's a danger. We don't know why she do all what she does, but the fact that she go inside a tantrum when she lose control, tell me that if she doesn't want control, she want a «statu quo».

Also, I don't know if she's well written, or if it's cliché, but I see immediately at the beginning what gonna happen next with Noriko.

I also see every traps she sow in the mind of Niki during the bath.

But, as I said, she's a danger. Not the antagonist. The antagonist of this story is the reset (or the gods). And I don't think she's the source of the reset.

But, she's a serious danger nonetheless. The fact that she follow Sensei through his phone (Maya know and it's official. I see a «Chekhov's gun» there, don't you?), create another level of danger.

That's all for me.

I don't get how I've read several comments of people praising Akira for shouting at Ami. Like, sure, I get why Akira shouted and was angry, and it does show that he's finally becoming suspicious of Ami's actions. Like, how can he be mad at Ami for leading Niki to Noriko and him since if he just kept it in his pants and didn't fuck his girlfriend's sister, none of the preceding events would have happened. Niki would have walked into the room, still suspicious, sure, but with nothing wrong having occurred.

He even says as much so that way he could feel like he put some amount of resistance in his failing backbone.

If he actually grew a spine, he'd have let Noriko down and not done what he did.

Sure, Ami did what she did for nefarious reasons, but that still doesn't change the fact that if Akira ACTUALLY had a spine, he wouldn't have fucked Noriko to begin with. Akira is not a hero for yelling at an obviously mentally broken girl who, as Niki says, needs some serious god damn help. And it ain't gonna be from the man who made her that way to begin with.

You may be misinterpreting the reaction. I think it's much less (or at all) that we think Akira is a hero, and much more that either 1. we (as readers) just want anyone to tell Ami off, or 2. that Akira's at least finally doing something.
A recurring complaint is that Akira does nothing at all, and we're tired of being glued to that sort of protagonist. In that sense, it doesn't matter if he's being hypocritical, because at least he has moved from inaction. Imo that's still a drop in the bucket, but it's definitely better than nothing.

In regard to him growing a spine, I actually noticed a lot of comments that more or less agree that (after understanding more about why he hasn't got a spine) are even more in favor of just castrating him for real (tacitly giving way to the beginning of a common understanding that he really might be beyond recovery and we ought to just be done with him).

Fucking Io faces her traumas better than him and she's a kid that was being raped forever by her own mother while her father did shit (at best).

I don't know where Selebus is going with this tbh, but I think he ought to reevaluate just to what extent he wishes to make his protagonist pathetic - lest he really kills any reason I have to care about him. Anyway, that's another topic.

Moonflare said:
I love Yuki. My reaction is just that I don't want to see people I love being brutally hurt. The girls and Akira hurt eachother under a cloak of consent. Their perception to what's being done is skewed, and thus more acceptable to the viewer - because they do it while thinking they're loving eachother while doing it.

This is one of the main points that Niki raises in this update: "Sure, now, it might seem like the potential damage is contained. But look at yourself, Akira, and tell me if decades later that remains true." The damage that they're doing to eachother takes a very long time to take effect to the extent that it would become clear. The immediate reaction of a young girl in a relationship with him doesn't seem that destructive by itself, it's just a very bad choice. But then, check back years later and that same girl had the opportunity to develop a healthy mindset taken from her, like Sara.

And after that conversation, I tend to think that Akira's right and maybe the rational thing here is chemical castration. Won't happen because this is an adult game and he's the protagonist, but logically it is a good choice. Not only for others, but to himself as well - as it would force him to develop other coping mechanisms (which could be a good thing with enough guidance).

I reacted very emotionally because there isn't any consent in Yuki's case. There's no "even though this isn't a good relationship choice, I still want it". There's just a shell of a woman, subjecting herself to abuse because she needs money for cancer treatment. Nothing about this softens the blow. In fact, Selebus thinks that isn't enough, and doubles down by having her gang-raped.

In the first half of the scene, Yuki's still in control, even though she hates what she's having to do. I think less people would have problems with that. Disgusting? yes. But within the bounds of what one can stomach to sit through. But the second part is just torture. She has no control, she's just a victim, and we have to watch her being broken beyond compare.

It's the sort of thing that is haunting and that I wish I didn't have to see. But we're all adults here, it's fiction, and we'll move past it.

Sign me up for that. It would be wild if that's what breaks Yumi's resistance and has her make a wish.

You're right that it is hypocritical, but it is also logical to hate someone that forced another to undergo surgery without anesthesia, when they could have had it. Which is basically the situation here.

It's not that she hurt Niki, or hurt Maya, or did whatever - it's the motivation. Akira really thought Ami has always had good intentions but horrid executions. When Akira realises this was to make Niki move out, and the thing with Maya was also orchestrated by her, he realises that Ami wears a facade. Thus the line:

View attachment 5001499

What overwrote Akira in regard to Ami is that she's this little girl that cares about nothing more than his happiness and that he has to protect. This is why she auto-wins anything in his mind. What happened here is that, for the first time, he realises that it is a facade. She has an agenda and has been manipulating everyone with glee.

This is not a full realisation yet, but there is a fragment here. And thus, Ami explodes. She reveals that she resents him to some extent for not being able to save Sekai from the gods. She reveals that what she does for him rivals, or likely goes beyond what Maya Prime ever did, and I think it's implied that it's more that he is the only thing left, than that she'd choose him in the first place.

She doesn't outright say it, because it doesn't need to be said: but she implies that Akira is pathetic and the multiplier, if not the source, of every issue she has. We could go further in the scene, but it would require an entire post.

posts.content_html_raw:
Doing a job after university really eats up my freeload time, xd. I've returned, and oh god, the 0.50 update was really heavy, but interesting nonetheless! Also I like how most of you just forgot about Sara x Sana events after Noriko x Niki x Ami and Yuki events. Anyway, here are my thoughts on 0.50:
Ayane is nice and kind, but it's kinda sad to see her sad as well. Yeah, thanks for supporting Sara, but anyway! Ayane is the only responsible person in the RAS thingie, considering Maya is dead, Sensei is Sensei, Yumi is deep in her own shit and Makoto being bitch about resets. I just... Why wouldn't they talk about it? I get it why Maya never did it, because she was a bitch about this and wanted to be cool (while not knowing anything and not even trying to do something). But why Makoto never did something? Because she accepted the shit? Bullshit! No way she would accept it. And I am not talking because she's smart, etc. Fuck it. I think it's just Sel not wanting to push the main plot before he deals with every single girl in the cast.

Sana x Sara events definitely lead us to a threesome, it's obvious. But once again, I do not like Sana's changes at all. For me it's too sudden and kinda... Unreasonably? I mean, even if she was a horny mess from the beginning, I'd like to see the changes way more prominent, then going from "I'm too shy to look at you" to "I wanna be knocked up by you" in a few updates without some middle land. Yeah, she had it, but it was kinda... meh?
Sara's shit is interesting though. Being a slut from the young age and never knowing a respect would make her agree to have a threesome with her own daughter just for gaining a little bit of "respect" from her... Sad reality.

The shit is hitting the ceiling... Poor Niki. As much as I pity her, I just can't feel too bad. Since knowing the game tendencies it will only lead to threesome between Nakayamas and Akira. Not soon but somewhere in 0.60s i think. Anyway, it's hot to finally see Noriko sex. But at what cost...

First of all, Yumi, since it's way more easier despite it being TTS. Pareidolia being a bitch and not knowing what the fuck just happened makes it funny. Though I'd like to see his reactions during TTS, not afterward comment. But I just hope Yumi won't use the "Happy" syringes and pills just like her mom did... (we can clearly see the drugs in Yumi's hand when "Sensei" appeared in front of her). Yumi is weak mentally, so she can fall into the temptation and try drugs. The only reason she doesn't do this because she saw all the consequences "thanks" to her mother. Something wants Yumi to lose her mind and just give into temptation? What if it is not about actual drugs but sex? IF so, please do not became another nymphomaniac, Yumi. It's kinda boring at this point.
Also I'm curious what does it mean to be tainted. Is that because she has Pareidolia inside her head? Or something else?
And what is that about her being far in the future where time is stopped? Is Sel implying how many years actually happened inside the loops? Or is that a hint that Yumi was something like Maya and Ami, surviving through a lot of cycles? HMM
Anyway, Yuki... This is hard shit. First two events were nice, especially when Kaori joined her. But the third one? I think Sel just wanted to make it as gruesome and brutal as possible. But it is like a horror-game. The more jumpscares you throw at player the less scary and more annoying it is. So is with Yuki's gangbang rape. Was it kind of disgusting? Yeah, it was bad. But it was bad is a sense of quality. Though finally seeing Yamaguchi patriarch is cool, but... Is this person a huge yakuza boss? More like a boss of some small thug clan, definitely non a biggest Yakuza organization.
I feel a lot of pity towards Yuki and I hope her life will change in a better position. All hope to Tsubasa. I wish she's not too horrible as a person.

In general, this update is... 7/10. Not the best, but really strong. Hits right into solar plexus. I don't have anything to say about Ami though. I just... it's the same shit over and over. She's always with a "cute and kind girl" mask under her "I don't think you are even a pet" personality. And there's always "but what if she don't? What if she is vulnerable person even deeper inside?" bullshit.
Oh, also. As much as I like Yumi, recently she has new events way too often I believe. But at least someone has to achieve some personality growth, right?

posts.content_html_raw:
Thought I might join the party and ramble about the update, though I'll skip mentioning Yuki's update, since it seems that everything that can be said has already been said
This is such a sweet moment between two characters that, quite frankly, haven't had enough screen time together. Not too much to add that hasn't been said already, but I'd like to highlight one comment that Ayane made, sorry no screenshot to go along with. She describes Akira as, "My stupid PREDATOR boyfriend", which if you ask me is a really great character growth moment for her. Confronting the truth of Akira's...erm, interests is an important stepping stone for her, and I personally hope that will eventually lead into her being a bit more assertive with Akira about his tendencies and how his self-destructive behavior is way more than just self-destructive. 10/10, no complaints
I'm not gonna lie, this section was rather disappointing for me. I wanted Sara to take a more assertive approach towards Sana after steeling her resolve, but that just didn't happen. After a bit of reflection, you know I just don't think that would have ever happened and would have been out of character for Sara's motivations and character tendencies. Adding onto a more explicit depiction of her abuse, and honestly it makes just as much sense for her to lack a backbone as Akira, seeing as it was literally beaten out of the both of them. (As an aside, I personally think that Akira and Sara would make for a fine romantic pair, seeing their shared struggle, but that's neither here nor there). What is definitely more intersting here is Sana's manipulation. It was pointed out previously in the thread that Sana's excuse of attempting to get closer with her mother is absolute horseshit. It was cruel. Full stop. Honestly, it was a power move to assert dominance over Sara knowing full well that her mother wouldn't assertively confront her about it after all she's been through. Seeing her "reconcile" with her mother with that sickly sweet fake smile makes my blood boil, and coupled with her previous admission that she's been sympathetic to Ami's possessiveness and has been having violent thoughts about the other girls getting close to Akira, she's been seeming rather...Ami-ish lately. Keep that in your mind, I'll return to that in a moment. 7/10 Well written...unfortunately
I'll personally skip the dynamic between Niki and Akira since it's been talked about a lot, and quite frankly makes me sad, so I'll skip straight to the Noriko/Akira situation. I'll start first with what I don't like in the writing. The story of Akira's abuse at the hands of Nozomu, love it. Fantastic. Well-written. Problem: I don't remember any point before this when Akira's memory of Nozomu returned to him. Several times before during Happy Moments or narrative events, portions of his memories of Sekai's abuse returned to Akira, and they were big moments in the story, and unless I'm not remembering properly or was way too drunk while playing, there never was any of that about Nozomu, which is a big deal, quite frankly as big of a deal as Sekai. Just dropping that out of nowhere seems really inappropriate to the audience, in a sort of horse-before-the-cart kind of narrative payoff without any buildup. 3/10. Moving on to the rest of the interaction between Noriko and Akira, there's one thing in particular that I want to point out. Noriko openly states that she knows that there's something going on between Maya (well, Maya Prime anyways) and Akira, even casually letting slip that she was jealous of Akira's and Maya's relationship way back then. You know, that kind of relationship. By all means this shouldn't be that big of a deal, except for the fact that was not at all what she said to Meat Puppet Maya back during Imani's first solo Dorm War. When she caught Meat Puppet Maya sneaking off to see Akira, she stopped her and was empathizing with her, and when Maya tried to rub her relationship with Akira in her face, Noriko sympathetically and with a shocked face said to her, "Maya...you got molested..." That's a whooooooole world of difference in language between these two moments, one that I can't call bad writing like I did the previous point. That feels intentional, like Noriko was attempting to manipulate Maya, and couple that with the fact that she didn't stay to try to own up to her behavior with Niki and how she invited Akira along clearly with impure intentions behind that sickly sweet smile and didn't take drastic measures to make sure that Niki wouldn't walk in on them, that feels rather...Ami-ish... you might see where I'm going with this, so keep that thought in your mind
Oh man, probably my favorite moment so far. Even when it's the result of her plan to hurt someone falling through, it just feels sooooooo cathartic to see basically the deuteragonist character at this point fully drop the cutesy tehe act and express how she feels without restraint or filter. It especially hits hard how technically all of her accusations towards Akira are all correct, even though each word is dripping with contempt for Niki (who is by all means a completely innocent character here) and everyone else getting in the way of her ultimate goal. That, plus her reveal to Akira that she knows about the Gods GODS gods, and oh man, what a moment. One thing in particular that I want to point out and theory craft on is the words she used. Yeah sure, we can talk about how huge of a departure it is for her to swear like a sailor like this or even get assertive at all, but I want to talk about how the word choice feels to me. It feels completely different to every line she's spoken except for the even where she NTRed Maya, the only other known event where she fully dropped the cutesy tehe act and spoke plainly. I don't have any screenshots of that even to pull, but calling back on my memory her word choice is, perhaps not more blunt since she's alway blunt, but quite a bit more direct, and always laced with a bit of grumpiness and rudeness that isn't really present in this way in any of her other lines. Her words are also strung together in a syntax that feels so radically different to every other line she's spoken. Even with the energy of the 0.50 crashout cranked all the way up to eleven, there's way more similarities in language between these two scenes than with others. And more importantly than this is the rhythm of her words that she uses in her crashout. There's something about the rising and falling emphasis on the syllables, at least how it sounds in my head, that makes her crashout sound, not necessarily exactly like Iambic Pentameter, but definitely something with a more refined and clear rhythm and beat. Ya know, like poetry. I'll skip the theory that Ami is Sekai, that although juicy and appealing to me is a bit more than I can chew off at the moment and instead posit that this moment is Ami's true personality: a grumpy rude teenage girl that's always tired of everyone's shit...so why not act like that all the time? To this we return to the fact that Ami knows about the gods and how they're attempting to make the perfect little porn game by inflicting enough trauma (sometime generational trauma) upon the characters to mold them into the perfect character archetypes of their intended trope. We've seen Ami talking to someone who wasn't truly there, albeit very briefly after the crashout where she cut her hair, and though it's not clear if she was speaking to Paredolia or Sekai (or whatever the hell may or may not be pretending to be Sekai), she herself is very clearly being messed with by the gods like most of the characters are, with the most alarming and explicit examples we know of being Sana, Sara, and Chika, each of whom has had a major personality change following their encounters. That would be how she went from a grumpy, rude, foul-mothed teenager into the cutesy incestuous yandere trope. It's a bit unclear to us how much Ami knows about how the gods are trying to manipulate her, or even worse if she's fully aware of what they're trying to do to her and is playing along in faith that she'll get Akira all to herself at the end of the process, but this moment where she fully abandonds the gods' chosen character archetype and lets loose has so many delicous narrative implications. Will this be the start of Ami rejecting the gods and joining the Rooftop Apocalypse Squad to try to get some kinds of agency back over their lives? Will Ami be punished by the gods for this "defiance" as Maya Prime thought to herself when she was trapped in a vision of her younger self, young Noriko, and Akira's "tutoring" session? Will Ami attempt to regain the favor of the gods and attempt to kill this particularly unruly Akira to try to start over again with a new Akira in the next cycle? Who know! All I know is that I'm excited for what the future holds. Either that, or I'm way overthinking things, but it makes me happy, so I don't care.
All in all, I'm quite satisfied with this update, in spite of its hiccups, and I'm cetainly glad to be sharing the way along this jouney with all of you guys. Still can't believe I was holding off on starting this game for the longest time.
