spoilers.title: Sana and Sara
spoilers.html: I'm not gonna lie, this section was rather disappointing for me. I wanted Sara to take a more assertive approach towards Sana after steeling her resolve, but that just didn't happen. After a bit of reflection, you know I just don't think that would have ever happened and would have been out of character for Sara's motivations and character tendencies. Adding onto a more explicit depiction of her abuse, and honestly it makes just as much sense for her to lack a backbone as Akira, seeing as it was literally beaten out of the both of them. (As an aside, I personally think that Akira and Sara would make for a fine romantic pair, seeing their shared struggle, but that's neither here nor there). What is definitely more intersting here is Sana's manipulation. It was pointed out previously in the thread that Sana's excuse of attempting to get closer with her mother is absolute horseshit. It was cruel. Full stop. Honestly, it was a power move to assert dominance over Sara knowing full well that her mother wouldn't assertively confront her about it after all she's been through. Seeing her "reconcile" with her mother with that sickly sweet fake smile makes my blood boil, and coupled with her previous admission that she's been sympathetic to Ami's possessiveness and has been having violent thoughts about the other girls getting close to Akira, she's been seeming rather...Ami-ish lately. Keep that in your mind, I'll return to that in a moment. 7/10 Well written...unfortunately

spoilers.title: Noriko and Akira
spoilers.html: I'll personally skip the dynamic between Niki and Akira since it's been talked about a lot, and quite frankly makes me sad, so I'll skip straight to the Noriko/Akira situation. I'll start first with what I don't like in the writing. The story of Akira's abuse at the hands of Nozomu, love it. Fantastic. Well-written. Problem: I don't remember any point before this when Akira's memory of Nozomu returned to him. Several times before during Happy Moments or narrative events, portions of his memories of Sekai's abuse returned to Akira, and they were big moments in the story, and unless I'm not remembering properly or was way too drunk while playing, there never was any of that about Nozomu, which is a big deal, quite frankly as big of a deal as Sekai. Just dropping that out of nowhere seems really inappropriate to the audience, in a sort of horse-before-the-cart kind of narrative payoff without any buildup. 3/10. Moving on to the rest of the interaction between Noriko and Akira, there's one thing in particular that I want to point out. Noriko openly states that she knows that there's something going on between Maya (well, Maya Prime anyways) and Akira, even casually letting slip that she was jealous of Akira's and Maya's relationship way back then. You know, that kind of relationship. By all means this shouldn't be that big of a deal, except for the fact that was not at all what she said to Meat Puppet Maya back during Imani's first solo Dorm War. When she caught Meat Puppet Maya sneaking off to see Akira, she stopped her and was empathizing with her, and when Maya tried to rub her relationship with Akira in her face, Noriko sympathetically and with a shocked face said to her, "Maya...you got molested..." That's a whooooooole world of difference in language between these two moments, one that I can't call bad writing like I did the previous point. That feels intentional, like Noriko was attempting to manipulate Maya, and couple that with the fact that she didn't stay to try to own up to her behavior with Niki and how she invited Akira along clearly with impure intentions behind that sickly sweet smile and didn't take drastic measures to make sure that Niki wouldn't walk in on them, that feels rather...Ami-ish... you might see where I'm going with this, so keep that thought in your mind

spoilers.title: Ami's Crashout
spoilers.html: Oh man, probably my favorite moment so far. Even when it's the result of her plan to hurt someone falling through, it just feels sooooooo cathartic to see basically the deuteragonist character at this point fully drop the cutesy tehe act and express how she feels without restraint or filter. It especially hits hard how technically all of her accusations towards Akira are all correct, even though each word is dripping with contempt for Niki (who is by all means a completely innocent character here) and everyone else getting in the way of her ultimate goal. That, plus her reveal to Akira that she knows about the Gods GODS gods, and oh man, what a moment. One thing in particular that I want to point out and theory craft on is the words she used. Yeah sure, we can talk about how huge of a departure it is for her to swear like a sailor like this or even get assertive at all, but I want to talk about how the word choice feels to me. It feels completely different to every line she's spoken except for the even where she NTRed Maya, the only other known event where she fully dropped the cutesy tehe act and spoke plainly. I don't have any screenshots of that even to pull, but calling back on my memory her word choice is, perhaps not more blunt since she's alway blunt, but quite a bit more direct, and always laced with a bit of grumpiness and rudeness that isn't really present in this way in any of her other lines. Her words are also strung together in a syntax that feels so radically different to every other line she's spoken. Even with the energy of the 0.50 crashout cranked all the way up to eleven, there's way more similarities in language between these two scenes than with others. And more importantly than this is the rhythm of her words that she uses in her crashout. There's something about the rising and falling emphasis on the syllables, at least how it sounds in my head, that makes her crashout sound, not necessarily exactly like Iambic Pentameter, but definitely something with a more refined and clear rhythm and beat. Ya know, like poetry. I'll skip the theory that Ami is Sekai, that although juicy and appealing to me is a bit more than I can chew off at the moment and instead posit that this moment is Ami's true personality: a grumpy rude teenage girl that's always tired of everyone's shit...so why not act like that all the time? To this we return to the fact that Ami knows about the gods and how they're attempting to make the perfect little porn game by inflicting enough trauma (sometime generational trauma) upon the characters to mold them into the perfect character archetypes of their intended trope. We've seen Ami talking to someone who wasn't truly there, albeit very briefly after the crashout where she cut her hair, and though it's not clear if she was speaking to Paredolia or Sekai (or whatever the hell may or may not be pretending to be Sekai), she herself is very clearly being messed with by the gods like most of the characters are, with the most alarming and explicit examples we know of being Sana, Sara, and Chika, each of whom has had a major personality change following their encounters. That would be how she went from a grumpy, rude, foul-mothed teenager into the cutesy incestuous yandere trope. It's a bit unclear to us how much Ami knows about how the gods are trying to manipulate her, or even worse if she's fully aware of what they're trying to do to her and is playing along in faith that she'll get Akira all to herself at the end of the process, but this moment where she fully abandonds the gods' chosen character archetype and lets loose has so many delicous narrative implications. Will this be the start of Ami rejecting the gods and joining the Rooftop Apocalypse Squad to try to get some kinds of agency back over their lives? Will Ami be punished by the gods for this "defiance" as Maya Prime thought to herself when she was trapped in a vision of her younger self, young Noriko, and Akira's "tutoring" session? Will Ami attempt to regain the favor of the gods and attempt to kill this particularly unruly Akira to try to start over again with a new Akira in the next cycle? Who know! All I know is that I'm excited for what the future holds. Either that, or I'm way overthinking things, but it makes me happy, so I don't care.

Everything said here is MY OPINION, anyone has the right to disagree with what was said, I just wanted to express MY OPINIONS about two characters.


Looking back at some events, I can only say one thing: Nodoka is much cooler than Ami.

Nodoka does bad things thinking they are good, and some of these things she doesn't realize are bad. In short, she does bad things thinking they are good for everyone involved.

Not Ami, she does a bad thing knowing it is bad, she doesn't care at all, she doesn't think it will result in anything positive for everyone involved, she is bad for completely selfish reasons, which will only benefit her and sometimes Akira (in her view) and no one else.

And another thing that's bothering me is seeing people easily believing Ami's words when she "blew up" with Akira, like, that could easily be her acting, everything she said she knew very well that it would hurt and mess up Akira's mind even more, they were words precisely chosen for that, she brought up the subject of him allowing her to call him father, she brought up the subject of Sekai, she brought up the gods, she brought up the problems of responsibilities that she had since she was young, everything was said exactly to hurt him. Yes, it could be her venting, but in my opinion, there's a 99% chance that everything she said was just a strategy of hers to make Akira feel more guilty, and get closer to her as a way of apologizing, until I see the complete unfolding of this event in the future, I won't think that it wasn't a strategy of hers and not her genuine feelings, Ami has reached a point where I can't believe what she says.

posts.content_html_raw:
Played the update yesterday and decided to let it stew as everything kind of sunk in and process. I'll start off using Moon's list of triggers to get everything organized and have everything out at once.

Ayane visiting a very depressed Sara was nice and the talk between them I really like, what I kind of was not a fan of was Sara's reaction and acceptance of what was happening and the way she justified it, I know and understand why and where she's coming from (Especially after seeing her past) But I feel there's something missing, nothing major or story altering but something that would fully connect the two points here that feels like they are only partially touching. Ayane's rant was nice as a way for her to vent and let something out.

The Ayane and Mikoto stuff was a bit of a fun break and nice little insight to what they have been doing. Ayane being headstrong into being friendly was nice, which I'm gonna need more of after what happens next.

Seeing Yumi talking to what ever it's name is made me curious on where that would go, her weird event happening and not being as trumatic as I thought, the two chalk board faces were interesting characters. Also what's his name being blocked out from what happened, did that also happen when it was talking to Sensei as well or has this been a Yumi thing only?

Following with Yuki and the apartment events, think this with Koari was one of the reasons I didn't immedietely close the game and quit it when that last event happened (More on this later) It was nice, and heart warming, and concerning when Sekai popped out. Also Akria trying to be a good person was a nice touch, not gonna lie after everything involving Yuki these past few updates I feared the worst with the knocking and was worried Akria had left her to dry by accident. Glad it wasn't the case.

The Maya event's weren't here or there for me, they felt like a nice move forward and bit more insight into new Maya and Ami's relationship now, it also has made me wonder just how much power does Ami really have during these loops. Sekai showing distain and loathing towards New Maya.

The beach trip I kind of predicted what would happen when Noriko invites Akira and he accepts and them being a lone together but damn I did not see it going that far and when Niki showed up for Akira to just, keep going like that, it makes sense the reason why but it was still a bit surprising. The following really made me feel for Niki, those feelings of hers breaking her further and further.

After getting home got hit with Ami insight and lore, Sekai suffering from the gods a year before she died which I think was touched on before, but Ami being aware of it and seeing and knowing it is happening to Akira. NGL those shots Sel did with both of them in frame opposites sides was quite impactful to the scene, him looking down and then the shift where Ami goes from the daughther he has to protect and make happy to someone he sees as a source of pain going fisheye lens was good, liked that. Can't wait to see where this will go and if Akira will start getting clued in that Ami is far more then she seems.

Now for that Yuki event, this event was rough cause I saw it happening from a mile away, I knew what was gonna go down the second I saw Yuki in that room, so I was able to prepare myself and with the previous Koari event was able to speed through it. After learning about her past in previous updates and her beating up the two Yakuza I knew and was able to brace myself, still took a day of letting it process for me to get past it (As much as one can) and those preview images of her new look also calmed me down a bit but fuck, I am hoping revenged is had in any way, cause if Sel decides to let them off scott free I will have to take a break for a while. I like Yuki a lot and was not comfortable seeing any of that. Was gonna close the game cause for the first time ever playing this game I underestimated how much it was gonna affect me and what headspace I was in (Some minor things happened yesterday that made me a bit down) until the Tsubasa scene which let me at least breath a small sigh of relief and release the tension I was feeling.

The Sara Sana stuff I'm iffy about, if Sel writes Sara fully embracing this and joining Sana as a weird family bonding and making herself happy then I can maybe see it as a good thing. If she's just self sacrificing and just doing it solely to make Sana happy while killing herself I'm gonna be very disappointed.

That's my thoughts so far, probably missing somethings but I'll just address them if someone brings it up either replying to me or I see a post that I wanna add to. Right now I need to find a Super fluffy porn game to clense myself, if only Twisted World updated or My New Memories was still able to be worked on I would probably of gone straight to those for some postitive comfort.

Since I haven't seen anyone else say it, but instead say
"here come the people saying to add an NTR tag ", I'll be the guy to say this officially needs an NTR tag. I had no issue with her sucking off her husband since
y'know
that's her husband
but getting gang raped by faceless npcs feels like a huge unnecessary disrespect and NTR rules in vns apply to ANY potential love interest, and can even be for important people in general. I get that it's iffy since it was nonconsensual, but I just want people to know that this game has that type of content, and it's not the first time, either. I had no problem tolerating it when it was between two other love interests, because we've done it with both of them and it's basically a matter of time before we do it with both at the same time anyway, so it's really irrelevant since like one of them implied, the mc wouldn't even mind anyway, or if anything, would encourage it.

My main issue isn't even that this happened to Yuki, if anything she should've known something like this or worse was coming after coming crawling back after swearing off it when she has half a dozen people now that she could very easily rely on, and I know it's not as easy to make that decision when in her state, but regardless, come the fuck on, Yuki.

My main issue lies in this opening the gate for worse things. Before it was just a little "haha it's ok cuz it's just a video on the computer during a reset, it didn't actually happen." "haha it's just Chiaki having a mental breakdown, it's not actually happening." and others I might have forgotten because they're insignificant by themselves.
It just feels like we're on a very subtle yet noticeable ramp until this point and now we get a full on gang rape scene with a character that's important to us, and that's not tolerable to everyone, so I leave this warning here for any newbies. At this point, I still recommend it, because this event in specific (unlike the other two mentioned) was reasonable and the character is married so "ntr" is to be expected, however I don't want this slippery slope to continue and I feel like Selebus is walking a tightrope and might lose fans over this one already.

Ayane - Ayane being best girl as always, nothing much new here

Sara - Happy for Sana to be able to groom her mother, I hate what Sana's become but at least if Sarah won't suffer as much for it, it'll be fine I guess.

Maya - Interesting to find out the boxes were actually Ami's all along, and getting closer to the flesh puppet Maya is always nice.

Yumi - Interesting to see Yumi as the first girl (iirc) that doesn't get invited to the symposium, wonder what makes her so impure compared to the other girls.

Niki - Same as Ayane, really hurts but good that she finally knows some of the truth and breaking up with Akira/losing 50 affection is incredible, only Queen Niki to finally do what so many other girls should have done a long time ago, shame it wasn't castration but it is what it is.

Yuki - Fucked up all around, no pun intended but very interesting that Tsubasa was just standing around coincidentally and apparently is her older sister?! The fact that they even know each other at all is curious, I'm assuming she only calls her that as an endearing term and not because they're literal family, but if they are that means Kaori is related to the Tsukiokas as well which would make this a whole entire thing.

Noriko - Great that she finally got what she wanted, and honestly more importantly than five hours of incestual sex, the fact that Sensei opened up to her with info that literally nobody else (that we know of) knows is so huge. Also nice for us to learn that info, but Noriko is more important than most people I mean look at her the poor thing, she's so cute us.
Shame it was interrupted by Ami's shenanigans but glad Sensei doubled down and didn't let her take this from Noriko a second time, girl was almost traumatized by the last one. Kind of surprised she took it in stride, but there's really not much else she could have done anyway, she can apologize to her sister for breaking a dozen sister laws when she's cooled off.

Ami - Glad both Ami and Sensei are finally trying to be human to each other for the first time in... ever probably? And actually having a discussion where one of them isn't playing it down or pretending everything is fine when it isn't. Families fight, and that argument was probably the best thing that happened to them since he started to be her dad instead of her uncle. They both have good reasons to be upset and pretending everything is fine isn't going to do either of them any good. Also funny that Sensei saw her as something evil and not his daughterniece for the first time. Wonder if anything actually changed due to her mother's influence or if this is just because she never made her sabotage this obvious and he's mad he didn't catch on earlier. Ami is so cute. I love my niece daughter.

Side note - hoooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooooly fuck Kittens 2 is insane. WOW. Peak. Best bonus content by far.

This TSS surprises me with the wrong reason. "Yumi's attendance is NOT required because she is tainted". Nani?!

To me, this indicates that TSS doesn't come from merely "universal reality decaying" (terminal 23 being increasing unstable), or "character lore dumping" at the audience like plenty of past happy events delivering information almost directly to the audience, as both of those more than likely should equally take effects onto all girls. As it turns out, some girls CAN be deemed less qualified than the others, and have to undergo a certain "patented curing" in order to fall in line with the others and proceed to the next step. So what does that mean when PA announced that Yumi is tainted? As in, tainted how? Comparing to other TSS girls, what distinguishes her from the rest?

Yumi being a part of the RAS doesn't work anymore because of Makoto. Yumi still being a virgin shouldn't work when Noriko and Sana at the same of their TSSs were also virgin as well. Yumi not being openly in love with Sensei is something on-brand to her among the current TSS girls, but it feels too shoujo manga to be an actual factor. Yumi still not having sexual encounter at any level with Sensei might work, but this would lead to making stretched rulings so that Noriko, the former queen of cockblocked, would not be counted as tainted by the time of her TSS. Yumi remembering stuff from other cycles when "Sensei wasn't Sensei" is also on-brand and could very much be the cause, though we just haven't figured out why she could remember anything.

Thus, personally, the easiest and the most straightforward solution for now is that Yumi currently has Pareidolia living inside her, something that makes her truly stand out from the previous five TSS girls (Pareidolia's conscious is even severed during TSS6). If such is true though, this would indirectly and further imply that there exists a behind-the-scene host for each and every TSS and this host denies girls infested with Pareidolia. Perhaps this host is one of the two remaining gods who has an agenda, its own ways of examining qualifications of each girl, different means to make girls cave (though this is only relatively obvious in the case of Sana and Chika), and possibly a goal in hope for achieving that somehow cannot be done through girls with divine infestation from other gods. Girls such as Yumi at her current state without some prerequisites will be unfit for this purpose.

Following this train of tinfoil thoughts, one of the most probable suspects who's behind TSSs would be HOPE. Among the rest of the known divines, the presence of many HOPE-related agents in different TSSs (youdidit, amiokay, angel1 and angel2) and HOPE's recent announced return really make HOPE feel like a BIG BAD from and a strong culprit behind these. This would also provide a roundabout reason why Sana, in comparison to Yumi, isn't consider tainted when this little sex gremlin also has her fair amount of divine influence inside her.

Regardless of whoever truly being any TSS, I just want to say FUCK YOU for swapping Yumi's candy in hand with THAT; feels especially triggering after knowing what has happened of Yuki in this update.

While I'm at it, FUCK those sea turtles too. How dare they make fun of her!

posts.content_html_raw:
Jeraviel said:
In practice I do think this event had the potential to be one of the best events despite the horrible things that happened in it. In fact I think even still the way it is, could have been a good event if Selebus simply stopped at the humiliation blowjob. It would have been one of those events that you hate to love it.

But instead he decided to add a gangrape on top of it, completely ruining for me. Not only did I left the event feeling bored, but Selebus also introduced a villain character that could have been interesting but then he went a ruined him (Yoshitsugu Yamaguchi) by making him into a caricature villain.

Is the same as with the Nozomu stuff. The Nozomu reveal was great because we got to learn more about how he treated his little brother, but that reveal would have also been ruined if it also turns out he raped Akira. Thanks god it didn't go that way, not because I care too much for Akira (which I actually do care for him), but because it would feel like an "artificial" way of making Akira's past more tragic. Instead I like the harmony between Nozomu & Sekai. One physically abused him, and the other sexually abused him. Is all about the balance.

Instead there was no balance to Yoshitsugu Yamaguchi. Not only that, he wasn't even developed to be an antagonist.
This whole time until know the impression I had of him is that he was a wimp with too much money. I didn't even know (or remember?) that he was the leader of the Yazuka in Kumon-Mi, I thought it was another family member (Yumi's grampa?)

I feel like there needed to be more build up towards his reveal and character. Is not like Selebus sucks at writing antagonists/villain-esque characters. we have Pareidolia, Sekai, Nozomu, Ami, Nodoka, Tsubasa, Sana (btw I'm using the term villain lightly, I know all of them are meant to be heroines minus Nozomu)
And yes Pareidolia is a heroine

Among those characters, god do I hate some of them and their actions, but I also love them for it.

But Yoshitsugu fell flat.
All we ever heard from him before was that he was a wimp who only dared to fuck Yuki when she was high on drugs, but that Yuki allowed him to do so because she could suck him out of his money to buy even more drugs.

But even without built up, this could have been a good introduction to him.

Up until the blowjob, I was kinda on his side. He was being an asshole, but you know, he was also talking to Yuki, someone who came to him multiple times just for his money so that she could get high. I don't blame him for assuming this was just a repeat for that. Him talking shit to Yuki and making her call him "Danna-sama" also makes sense. He is meant to be the boss of a Yakuza family, he cannot show any sign of weakness in front of his men.

Even after the blowjob I was like "He is a piece of shit, but damn this guy actually means business." making Yuki give him a blowjob and about cutting that other Yakuza guy's finger for messing around his wife. It was a clash of pride vs pride.

but then the whole gangrape and without paying her happened and he simply went from a "could-be-interesing villain" to cartoonishly evil character. It just a fucking stupid development because it also degrades Yoshitsugu's position.

The point of the blowjob wasn't that he wanted to humiliate Yuki, but instead it was a powerplay to show everyone the dragon was tamed by him. It went from "Everyone here, look and respect me, the one who made the dragon service me" to a cuck that passed his wife around. She went from being a dragon to just becoming a whore. If I had to guess then that last sentence was the whole point of the event, that "Yuki is no longer The Dragon but instead someone who needs help" but that message could have been conveyed without the unnecessary gangrape.

Maybe this wasn't Selebus's intention, but now it feels like Yoshitsugu and the whole Yazuka men exist only make Akira look good in comparison. If that was his intention then he kinda fails because honestly, Yoshitsugu might be a piece of shit but at least he has more spine than Akira lol
Click to expand...
Agreed on Yuki's event. If it had stopped at the BJ, this would have been a solid, if dark, 9/10 update for me. Instead, everything else was completely overshadowed and it became an IDidn'tSignUpForThisShit/10 update and leaves me feeling dread rather than anticipation for future updates. Even if this outcome was realistic given the situation (debatable), I don't like that the situation was written so this could be the outcome.

With other characters who had similar rape events, aside from that Ami/Maya scene, there were still enough degrees of separation - backstory, world-ending weirdness, dreams, etc. - that I could still compartmentalize and accept it. But this event was different, and I'm certain that whatever narrative beat Sel wanted it to accomplish in the future could have been accomplished without.

Guess we'll see how the next few updates pan out, but this one event sure took a lot of the enjoyment out the game for me. I'm not even mad about it anymore, just sad, disappointed, and worried about what the future of this game may hold.

spoilers.title: TSS6
spoilers.html:
This TSS surprises me with the wrong reason. "Yumi's attendance is NOT required because she is tainted". Nani?!

To me, this indicates that TSS doesn't come from merely "universal reality decaying" (terminal 23 being increasing unstable), or "character lore dumping" at the audience like plenty of past happy events delivering information almost directly to the audience, as both of those more than likely should equally take effects onto all girls. As it turns out, some girls CAN be deemed less qualified than the others, and have to undergo a certain "patented curing" in order to fall in line with the others and proceed to the next step. So what does that mean when PA announced that Yumi is tainted? As in, tainted how? Comparing to other TSS girls, what distinguishes her from the rest?

Yumi being a part of the RAS doesn't work anymore because of Makoto. Yumi still being a virgin shouldn't work when Noriko and Sana at the same of their TSSs were also virgin as well. Yumi not being openly in love with Sensei is something on-brand to her among the current TSS girls, but it feels too shoujo manga to be an actual factor. Yumi still not having sexual encounter at any level with Sensei might work, but this would lead to making stretched rulings so that Noriko, the former queen of cockblocked, would not be counted as tainted by the time of her TSS. Yumi remembering stuff from other cycles when "Sensei wasn't Sensei" is also on-brand and could very much be the cause, though we just haven't figured out why she could remember anything.

Thus, personally, the easiest and the most straightforward solution for now is that Yumi currently has Pareidolia living inside her, something that makes her truly stand out from the previous five TSS girls (Pareidolia's conscious is even severed during TSS6). If such is true though, this would indirectly and further imply that there exists a behind-the-scene host for each and every TSS and this host denies girls infested with Pareidolia. Perhaps this host is one of the two remaining gods who has an agenda, its own ways of examining qualifications of each girl, different means to make girls cave (though this is only relatively obvious in the case of Sana and Chika), and possibly a goal in hope for achieving that somehow cannot be done through girls with divine infestation from other gods. Girls such as Yumi at her current state without some prerequisites will be unfit for this purpose.

Following this train of tinfoil thoughts, one of the most probable suspects who's behind TSSs would be HOPE. Among the rest of the known divines, the presence of many HOPE-related agents in different TSSs (youdidit, amiokay, angel1 and angel2) and HOPE's recent announced return really make HOPE feel like a BIG BAD from and a strong culprit behind these. This would also provide a roundabout reason why Sana, in comparison to Yumi, isn't consider tainted when this little sex gremlin also has her fair amount of divine influence inside her.

Regardless of whoever truly being any TSS, I just want to say FUCK YOU for swapping Yumi's candy in hand with THAT; feels especially triggering after knowing what has happened of Yuki in this update.

While I'm at it, FUCK those sea turtles too. How dare they make fun of her!

fdsasdf_p said:
[Yumi's TSS]
Click to expand...
Though I have, from the start, speculated the connection between being tainted and Pareidolia - I have not elaborated on that. So I'll also take the opportunity to build upon what you said.

Edit: It's a whole lot of questions without answers, so you guys can skip it if you want.
I agree that if Pareidolia's being blocked from the TSS, we can safely assume he's not related to it. Which would mean that previous theories of the "Replica of heaven", where Maya Prime is at currently, has nothing to do with him. So he really didn't save, nor would be able to save her anyway.

Furthermore, that Sekaori can walk around in multiple TSS's would mean that Sekaori is not comparable to Pareidolia in terms of privilege (it would appear she's higher, at least in this regard).

Continuing with this, Sekaori directly talks to Sana during her TSS, and seems to point to the fact that she doesn't want to be the one to erase her. Then, during the short period that Pareidolia inhabits Kaori, we can now also confirm that it was only for a short while indeed. What does all this mean, though? Because we thought that Kaori might be able to erase her because of Pareidolia's authority, which Himawari fears.

But now, we have Himawari < Pareidolia < Sekaori < Actual gods of the TSS. Or not, this is all speculation.

Another bit of speculation is what is Pareidolia's state. Now that we have confirmed he's with Yumi, how is that possible? Pareidolia (the concerned) was a being born out of Akira's childhood, for him only. That was his whole thing. So how could he piggyback to Yumi (once he sacrificed himself to reveal the truth of the gods to Akira?). Furthermore, Pareidolia, whilst with Akira, was in control of Spring. He doesn't seem to control shit now.

Yet, he was supposed to be the one that was controlling Sana, right? At least it seemed like he was responsible for making her "bloom". Maybe the whole theory about actually being HOPE the one behind that is true? I say this because, on the green path, Sara also has started to "bloom" (there is a mention of this in the last Sara 3). And Pareidolia has nothing to do with it.

All of this throws the idea of Pareidolia into even more confusion. The idea of "Pareidolia will have my head for this" during "Miserably ever after", Himawari actually running away from him (whilst in Kaori's body) on the rooftop - and yet, right now, he seems to be able to do nothing... What is it that they're fearing? Is it that his position used to grant him power and now he has nothing?

And after all of these questions...
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
I'd just like to say that I deeply appreciated the candy stuff in Yumi's TSS. Because, well, the metaphor is amazing. "Candy" as in actual candy is a great symbol of childhood for a girl that 1. suffers from lack of food, 2. lost an actual ancestry of running a candy shop, 3. has zero sweetness/fond memories of a innocent "sugary" childhood.

So for the solution to be for her "to finally have candy" makes complete sense if you look at it as an adult Yumi compensating for a childhood that was lost. But then it shifts into candy being drugs. And that's also amazing in its darkness. Not only in the sense of actual drugs, as Deskel once pointed out on being sort of expected of someone in Yumi's position - but also in the sense that if she started to "compensate" for what she lost, she'd likely lose herself in that need regardless.

Even if Yumi were not to go into drugs, anything can become a drug to her - most obviously Akira. A person that'd "be there", "affection" through sexual intercourse, these would all fill in the gap, and her need is great. After all, this was most likely the case for the original Akira to get so invested in her (for overall benign intentions or not), the fact that she's the perfect target. Anyway, I thought it was a great metaphor.

Furthermore, that Sekaori can walk around in multiple TSS's would mean that Sekaori is not comparable to Pareidolia in terms of privilege (it would appear she's higher, at least in this regard).

Continuing with this, Sekaori directly talks to Sana during her TSS, and seems to point to the fact that she doesn't want to be the one to erase her. Then, during the short period that Pareidolia inhabits Kaori, we can now also confirm that it was only for a short while indeed. What does all this mean, though? Because we thought that Kaori might be able to erase her because of Pareidolia's authority, which Himawari fears.

But now, we have Himawari < Pareidolia < Sekaori < Actual gods of the TSS. Or not, this is all speculation.

Another bit of speculation is what is Pareidolia's state. Now that we have confirmed he's with Yumi, how is that possible? Pareidolia (the concerned) was a being born out of Akira's childhood, for him only. That was his whole thing. So how could he piggyback to Yumi (once he sacrificed himself to reveal the truth of the gods to Akira?). Furthermore, Pareidolia, whilst with Akira, was in control of Spring. He doesn't seem to control shit now.

Yet, he was supposed to be the one that was controlling Sana, right? At least it seemed like he was responsible for making her "bloom". Maybe the whole theory about actually being HOPE the one behind that is true? I say this because, on the green path, Sara also has started to "bloom" (there is a mention of this in the last Sara 3). And Pareidolia has nothing to do with it.

All of this throws the idea of Pareidolia into even more confusion. The idea of "Pareidolia will have my head for this" during "Miserably ever after", Himawari actually running away from him (whilst in Kaori's body) on the rooftop - and yet, right now, he seems to be able to do nothing... What is it that they're fearing? Is it that his position used to grant him power and now he has nothing?

And after all of these questions...

A person that'd "be there", "affection" through sexual intercourse, these would all fill in the gap, and her need is great. After all, this was most likely the case for the original Akira to get so invested in her (for overall benign intentions or not), the fact that she's the perfect target. Anyway, I thought it was a great metaphor.

Piracy aside, I think a lot of the problems come from who Selebus is as a person (or what he turned into). Let's examine the puzzles, for instance.
The Last Sovereign is a game that, debatably, plays better with extensive support. The story is an ever changing reflection of your choices, and there are so many and complex ones (regarding investments for example), that you only see the result of 20 hours after the fact, or even longer.

Now think about this from a developer pov, do you think that Sierra Lee (the dev) spent her time developing a game that would need a walkthrough to play? Obviously not. She most likely delighted in creating paths that would come as a surprise to the player as a reflection of their past choices as they naturally move through the game. But some people just want to be guided through things. What is she to do then? Prohibit the general user (or even worse, her patrons) from using walkthroughs?

Of course not, she encourages it - as any sane person would do. Because, after all, you can play her game however you want. Is she perfect in this regard? Also no, because there are a few points where if you cheated (like giving your character absurd amounts of health, or clearing a boss faster than it should be possible), the game will punish you (very mildly) for it. But it's definitely better than Selebus.

Selebus actively prohibits, ridicules and bans people that offer puzzle solutions, and yet states that you can make LiL to be whatever you want. The issue (and origin of this dissonance), in my view, is that Selebus has an overblown idea of what Lessons in Love is. He views his product as art, and there's nothing wrong with that, but he falls short both of understanding the medium through which that art is delivered (a game) and the overall freedom that should follow a statement of "make of it what you want".

What he means by that statement (as confirmed in a number of his event commentaries) is that you can interpret the story of LiL however you want. Even though he will also ridicule people for not conforming to his vision regarding that too (when he addresses such theories in-game, like the plant councils). He does not however think you should be able to play how you want.

I can only surmise that Selebus thinks (to some level) that being able to experience LiL is a prize, not a right. That's the logic behind banning people from sharing puzzle guides: "if you can't find your way through the challenges, you're not worthy of continuing the journey". And that's just, imo, pretentious bullshit (and also confusing since he supports the wiki).

I praise this game a lot, but let me state something that (in this light) needs to be said. Lessons in Love has many flaws, including its narrative and overall writing. Selebus is not writing the transcendental piece that will shift the human paradigm forward a hundred years. And even if that were the case, it would be the more reason to encourage more people to play it, rather than less (with his puzzle policy).

Thus, for all the flaws Lessons in Love has, Selebus has even more. Because a game, any game, cannot be perfect - and it often falls to the community to rally and fix those flaws by themselves for themselves. That is the case of the walkthrough mod, the puzzle guides, and (to a lesser extent) my own trigger guides. But what Selebus does, paradoxically, is to forbid his own community from helping itself (regarding puzzles at least).
TLDR is: Piracy or not, were I to join the discord and publish my trigger guides a couple hours after release (or ever), I'd be banned. The real issue is Selebus himself.

Let it be known that I've examined puzzles specifically. Way more can be said about other systems and behaviors from the dev - but you guys can extrapolate from what I wrote.

spoilers.title: TLS vs LiL
spoilers.html:
The Last Sovereign is a game that, debatably, plays better with extensive support. The story is an ever changing reflection of your choices, and there are so many and complex ones (regarding investments for example), that you only see the result of 20 hours after the fact, or even longer.

Now think about this from a developer pov, do you think that Sierra Lee (the dev) spent her time developing a game that would need a walkthrough to play? Obviously not. She most likely delighted in creating paths that would come as a surprise to the player as a reflection of their past choices as they naturally move through the game. But some people just want to be guided through things. What is she to do then? Prohibit the general user (or even worse, her patrons) from using walkthroughs?

Of course not, she encourages it - as any sane person would do. Because, after all, you can play her game however you want. Is she perfect in this regard? Also no, because there are a few points where if you cheated (like giving your character absurd amounts of health, or clearing a boss faster than it should be possible), the game will punish you (very midly) for it. But it's definitely better than Selebus.

Selebus actively prohibits, ridicules and bans people that offer puzzle solutions, and yet states that you can make LiL to be whatever you want. The issue (and origin of this dissonance), in my view, is that Selebus has an overblown idea of what Lessons in Love is. He views his product as art, and there's nothing wrong with that, but he falls short both of understanding the medium through which that art is delivered (a game) and the overall freedom that should follow a statement of "make of it what you want".

What he means by that statement (as confirmed in a number of his event commentaries) is that you can interpret the story of LiL however you want. Even though he will also ridicule people for not conforming to his vision regarding that too (when he addresses such theories in-game, like the plant councils). He does not however think you should be able to play how you want.

I can only surmise that Selebus thinks (to some level) that being able to experience LiL is a prize, not a right. That's the logic behind banning people from sharing puzzle guides: "if you can't find your way through the challenges, you're not worthy of continuing the journey". And that's just, imo, pretentious bullshit (and also confusing since he supports the wiki).

I praise this game a lot, but let me state something that (in this light) needs to be said. Lessons in Love has many flaws, including its narrative and overall writing. Selebus is not writing the transcendental piece that will shift the human paradigm forward a hundred years. And even if that were the case, it would be the more reason to encourage more people to play it, rather than less (with his puzzle policy).

Thus, for all the flaws Lessons in Love has, Selebus has even more. Because a game, any game, cannot be perfect - and it often falls to the community to rally and fix those flaws by themselves for themselves. That is the case of the walkthrough mod, the puzzle guides, and (to a lesser extent) my own trigger guides. But what Selebus does, paradoxically, is to forbid his own community from helping itself (regarding puzzles at least).

Mike.Ross80 said:
I like how the BaDIK creator handles guides, where I think it is like a month after release, a full walkthrough is provided to patreon followers but then gets posted elsewhere but he dont make a peep about it at all.
Click to expand...
I think it's just an obvious move to provide your supporters with a full walkthrough - because it's an added benefit for them with almost no cost to you (if it's built in-game, obviously that demands more work).
But in the case of a pdf...I mean, you already know how to play your game, you set everything up. What's the issue? Taking 5 minutes to write everything down? Devs that don't do this are either missing out, have a game that don't need it, or are wrong in the head.

In regard to supporters leaking stuff, that's the dev's prerogative. I, personally, don't think I'd mind. Especially regarding walkthroughs. The way I see it, a supporter is not paying for perks, they're paying so that the game continues being made. So if they want to share their perks, it is up to them.

I think that positive messaging works better in this case. A dev could make their official position that "if you didn't pay for this, I'd appreciate if you could help with advertising it" or something. There are a couple of options in that tone that ought to do better than the obvious "you should be paying for this!" - because that does nothing.

Moonflare said:
Piracy aside, I think a lot of the problems come from who Selebus is as a person (or what he turned into). Let's examine the puzzles, for instance.
The Last Sovereign is a game that, debatably, plays better with extensive support. The story is an ever changing reflection of your choices, and there are so many and complex ones (regarding investments for example), that you only see the result of 20 hours after the fact, or even longer.

Now think about this from a developer pov, do you think that Sierra Lee (the dev) spent her time developing a game that would need a walkthrough to play? Obviously not. She most likely delighted in creating paths that would come as a surprise to the player as a reflection of their past choices as they naturally move through the game. But some people just want to be guided through things. What is she to do then? Prohibit the general user (or even worse, her patrons) from using walkthroughs?

Of course not, she encourages it - as any sane person would do. Because, after all, you can play her game however you want. Is she perfect in this regard? Also no, because there are a few points where if you cheated (like giving your character absurd amounts of health, or clearing a boss faster than it should be possible), the game will punish you (very midly) for it. But it's definitely better than Selebus.

Selebus actively prohibits, ridicules and bans people that offer puzzle solutions, and yet states that you can make LiL to be whatever you want. The issue (and origin of this dissonance), in my view, is that Selebus has an overblown idea of what Lessons in Love is. He views his product as art, and there's nothing wrong with that, but he falls short both of understanding the medium through which that art is delivered (a game) and the overall freedom that should follow a statement of "make of it what you want".

What he means by that statement (as confirmed in a number of his event commentaries) is that you can interpret the story of LiL however you want. Even though he will also ridicule people for not conforming to his vision regarding that too (when he addresses such theories in-game, like the plant councils). He does not however think you should be able to play how you want.

I can only surmise that Selebus thinks (to some level) that being able to experience LiL is a prize, not a right. That's the logic behind banning people from sharing puzzle guides: "if you can't find your way through the challenges, you're not worthy of continuing the journey". And that's just, imo, pretentious bullshit (and also confusing since he supports the wiki).

I praise this game a lot, but let me state something that (in this light) needs to be said. Lessons in Love has many flaws, including its narrative and overall writing. Selebus is not writing the transcendental piece that will shift the human paradigm forward a hundred years. And even if that were the case, it would be the more reason to encourage more people to play it, rather than less (with his puzzle policy).

Thus, for all the flaws Lessons in Love has, Selebus has even more. Because a game, any game, cannot be perfect - and it often falls to the community to rally and fix those flaws by themselves for themselves. That is the case of the walkthrough mod, the puzzle guides, and (to a lesser extent) my own trigger guides. But what Selebus does, paradoxically, is to forbid his own community from helping itself (regarding puzzles at least).
TLDR is: Piracy or not, were I to join the discord and publish my trigger guides a couple hours after release (or ever), I'd be banned. The real issue is Selebus himself.

Let it be known that I've examined puzzles specifically. Way more can be said about other systems and behaviors from the dev - but you guys can extrapolate from what I wrote.
Click to expand...
I've known Selebus for a long time, and I know that the reason why Akira is so well written as a self-destructive character is because he himself is a self-destructive person, there's nobody else who can understand this feeling, but the funniest thing is that he's either completely oblivious to it or refuses to admit it.
He thinks he's a writing genius when all he does is take his own disgusting persona and mold it into what he wishes people saw in him: Someone who's "Misunderstood".
In a way, he succeeded. Akira is a tragic character, a disgusting and vile one, and despite all of it, everyone still likes him.
The tragedy of Selebus is that this is not a fantasy, and he himself won't be liked for his own unpleasant personality.

On the topic of Ami: something interesting that I noticed about last update is that it seemed like Chapter 1 to 3 Ami had no clue about the boxes and was bothered by the idea of it:

Sensei - "What is it with you two and getting me to carry stuff across town this late at night?"
Ami - "It's not 'across town' Sensei, it's like two blocks-"
- "Wait. What did you just say?"
Sensei - "I said that you are lucky I'm feeling generous tonight. Because otherwise, I would not do this."
Ami - "..."
- "Okay!"
(Chapter 1 Ami 'Back Out in the Heat' Event)
Way later:

Ami - "Would you have preferred to 'have a talk' with Sensei in my place? Would you have preferred to have him 'help you carry stuff?'"
(Chapter 3 'I Won't Say I'm In Love' Main Event)
She's also probably referring to the Chapter 2 Maya 'Stop Looking For Answers' Event where she and Sensei have a talk about something. This event also bothered Ayane.

Meanwhile; current Chapter 4 Ami seems to know everything about the boxes and might even be responsible for them:

New Maya - "Because of fucking Ami!"
- "She keeps leaving these fucking boxes in there and refuses to move them herself."
Sensei Narrator - "But to figure out what this is. And how Ami is somehow involved now."
- "Why would she ask Maya to take this here? Why can't Maya open it either?"
- "Was that...always how it worked?"
(Chapter 4 Maya 'Billy Pilgrim' Event)

New Maya - "Yeah! Maybe if you didn't also fucking tell me that the reason I had to do your stupid, box-based chores was because you were busy!"
Ami - "Oh yeah. I did say that, didn't I? Wow. Maybe I am the bad guy here after all then?"
- "Well...think about it. If I don't tell you to dispose of that box, Sensei's never rocked by his emotional connection to it."
- "Then the two of you don't use the rest of the night to start repairing the broken bridge that is your relationship and go eat takoyaki and stuff."
(Chapter 4 Maya 'My Perfect World' Event)
She even seemed to use the boxes to get New Maya and Sensei closer to eachother, enabling Sensei to somewhat move on from Maya Prime, and spend more time with New Maya. The boxes were effectively used as a tool by current Ami.

Overall: Chapter 1 to 3 Ami at least acted bothered by the idea of Sensei carrying something for Maya. Chapter 4 casually uses the very idea as a tool to develop their feelings for eachother.

Bingoogus said:
The reason i enjoy LiL is the subject matter, you just can't get this kind of story outside of places like this, normies would react with extreme rhetorical violence. Now don't get me wrong, i love porn games too, but the one thing i craved for years was adult stories, true adult stories, for adults, where normal shit like sex doesn't just fade to a black screen or skip to after.

Now, all of us are complete fucking nerds, so i've no doubt some of you are virgins, but even then, we all know sex is a normal part of being an adult, and as adults, we can enjoy fiction without having to be concerned with moral implications of consuming it. I want to read stories about fucked up people and fucked up situations, not because i'm fucked up (i am) but because it's the one kind of thing you can't find in the mainstream pile, you have to find the hidden nooks and crannies to find content like LiL. I'm not a teenager, haven't been for almost two decades, and i just want to consume content appropriate for my age, that is, everything, and not have censors tell me no.

LiL has plenty of sex in it, but almost none of it is hot, but it exists and is normalized within the story, i appreciate that fact, it has a story to tell and it doesn't fade to black cause of censorship. Reading a story about the cycle of childhood sexual abuse mixed with mindfuckery is exactly the kind of fucked up stuff i wished existed before i found this site.
Click to expand...
First of all, ow my already weak mentality and heart. Second, I really do have to agree, I really love stories about testing the limits of humanity and how far are people willing to go, it only makes them shine better when they do come out the other side cleaner than they started. You think with so many shows and movies out right now, there'll be at least a decent amount covering it but not really; it's hard to bring those topics to light and personally, I think the more forbidden and harder to discuss about should be hidden in the dark corners of the internet. With more censors than ever and more corporations buying out creativity and draining it out in droves, I think it's nice in a fucked up sort of way to find creavity in the darkness of humanity, and to be able to discuss with fairly likeminded people like everyone here (you're all surprising great and not fucked up people), I certainly didn't expect to find it in a porn game of all places to be honest with the rest of you.

Moonflare said:
Piracy aside, I think a lot of the problems come from who Selebus is as a person (or what he turned into). Let's examine the puzzles, for instance.
The Last Sovereign is a game that, debatably, plays better with extensive support. The story is an ever changing reflection of your choices, and there are so many and complex ones (regarding investments for example), that you only see the result of 20 hours after the fact, or even longer.

Now think about this from a developer pov, do you think that Sierra Lee (the dev) spent her time developing a game that would need a walkthrough to play? Obviously not. She most likely delighted in creating paths that would come as a surprise to the player as a reflection of their past choices as they naturally move through the game. But some people just want to be guided through things. What is she to do then? Prohibit the general user (or even worse, her patrons) from using walkthroughs?

Of course not, she encourages it - as any sane person would do. Because, after all, you can play her game however you want. Is she perfect in this regard? Also no, because there are a few points where if you cheated (like giving your character absurd amounts of health, or clearing a boss faster than it should be possible), the game will punish you (very midly) for it. But it's definitely better than Selebus.

Selebus actively prohibits, ridicules and bans people that offer puzzle solutions, and yet states that you can make LiL to be whatever you want. The issue (and origin of this dissonance), in my view, is that Selebus has an overblown idea of what Lessons in Love is. He views his product as art, and there's nothing wrong with that, but he falls short both of understanding the medium through which that art is delivered (a game) and the overall freedom that should follow a statement of "make of it what you want".

What he means by that statement (as confirmed in a number of his event commentaries) is that you can interpret the story of LiL however you want. Even though he will also ridicule people for not conforming to his vision regarding that too (when he addresses such theories in-game, like the plant councils). He does not however think you should be able to play how you want.

I can only surmise that Selebus thinks (to some level) that being able to experience LiL is a prize, not a right. That's the logic behind banning people from sharing puzzle guides: "if you can't find your way through the challenges, you're not worthy of continuing the journey". And that's just, imo, pretentious bullshit (and also confusing since he supports the wiki).

I praise this game a lot, but let me state something that (in this light) needs to be said. Lessons in Love has many flaws, including its narrative and overall writing. Selebus is not writing the transcendental piece that will shift the human paradigm forward a hundred years. And even if that were the case, it would be the more reason to encourage more people to play it, rather than less (with his puzzle policy).

Thus, for all the flaws Lessons in Love has, Selebus has even more. Because a game, any game, cannot be perfect - and it often falls to the community to rally and fix those flaws by themselves for themselves. That is the case of the walkthrough mod, the puzzle guides, and (to a lesser extent) my own trigger guides. But what Selebus does, paradoxically, is to forbid his own community from helping itself (regarding puzzles at least).
TLDR is: Piracy or not, were I to join the discord and publish my trigger guides a couple hours after release (or ever), I'd be banned. The real issue is Selebus himself.

Let it be known that I've examined puzzles specifically. Way more can be said about other systems and behaviors from the dev - but you guys can extrapolate from what I wrote.
Click to expand...
Tbh, this made me want to try The Last Sovereign more than ever and you made me honestly want to have another go at it again blind to see if I can get into it, if you got any more games to advertise I would love to know.

In other words, you really summed up my problems with Selebus as a person and with his work, really have nothing more to say about the guy that hasn't been said here already in this forum.

I think that summarized what was wrong with yuki's events in a nice bow honestly imo.
Stomache is central to Io's character, we understood what illed her after numerous of updates as we got know her, and people liked her for weaknesses and her weirdness so when stomache happened and not only confirmed what we expected but forced us to be in the same role as their captors, everything went crumbling down, so did we; but Yuki's events were written out of nowhere from the story's perspective, it felt all so artificial, it feel fake, like I get it, you wanted to create tension, a dark moment and stain in yuki's history and force the story into a direction that you needed it to go, you need an event like that and break yuki to her lowest's point but there wasn't any buildup, it was overblown with all cruelity that it made it more ridiculous than emotional gut wrenching.

With Stomache I couldn't play the game or come back to this forum for weeks, that fucking two choice prompt broke me, with yuki, I said to ask myself "really?"

Again as this game is in a work in progress and the event is still new in everyones' minds, this issue could be explained or addressed or not that big in the grand scheme of things, but as of rn, the event disappoints me.

posts.content_html_raw:
I still hold hope for Akira, even if it has been tougher to do so lately.

He’s gotten on the right track a few times, such as when he opened up about Sekai to Maki and Io or Nozomu with Noriko, but the thing is… he self-sabotages his own growth.

Why? Because he feels guilty.

Guilty about not going to Kyoto with Sekai and ignoring the warning signs of the voices in her head prior to her death. In his mind, he is responsible.

“Why do I deserve to be happy, when she couldn’t?”

That, I believe, is Akira’s mindset. He starts to enjoy some aspect of his life, then when it becomes too much, he sets it on fire.

Take this recent Niki situation for example. He very well could have a nice life with her… He’d have someone utterly devoted to him who’s known him for years, be financially set for life, and have a new mother figure for Ami. It would be perfect.

…Only not really, because then that would be effectively erasing Sekai’s influence, now wouldn’t it? Over Akira and Ami both. And what happens to a god when their influence wanes? They become less powerful, until eventually, they cease to exist entirely. (Sounds almost like a hint for what needs to happen or something.)

Akira will need to face his trauma head on eventually if this game is to ever reach a satisfying conclusion. Sekai, Nozomu, his parents. All of it.

Perhaps Wakana will be able to help out with this in the next update. It would be strange if her investigation just went nowhere after all this time. She’s honestly in a pretty unique position.

We may be disappointed in him right now (I still feel bad for Niki and Sara), but hey. It’s Chapter 4. It kinda comes with the territory.
Still holding out hope for the next Beach update in September. With all the foreshadowing that’s been going on, there’s no way we don’t get some answers on all this weirdness.

I for one still don’t buy that this current Ami is even the one we’re familiar with at all. As Akira realized last update during their conversation, this Ami is out to hurt him. Something that the Ami we know would never do.

Just look back at Ami’s “Della” event. In the midst of her mental breakdown, as soon as she stabbed Akira with the scissors, she immediately froze and looked terrified about it.

Somehow? I doubt this current Ami would care all that much. She’d probably just justify it like, “Oh well, he can just be reset and come back anyway!”.

I dunno. Maybe Tsubasa can offer some insight in 0.51 during her events. She seems to know a lot.
